stories.title: LPG crisis across India:Cooking shifts to roadside stoves; rush at coal and firewood stores, consumers queue outside gas agencies
stories.summary: Disruptions in gas supply have created difficulties for both commercial establishments and domestic consumers. In response to the situation, the government has cancelled the leave of officials and staff in the Food Department. Special teams have also been formed to conduct raids and prevent black marketing of gas cylinders. In Udaipur, authorities seized several cylinders during an operation against illegal refilling. At the same time, hotels and restaurants in multiple cities are beginning to suspend operations as their gas stock runs out. Meanwhile, the Congress party has announced a two-day protest at district headquarters starting today to oppose the rise in gas prices. Illegal refilling racket busted in Udaipur In Udaipur city, a team from the district administration seized six cylinders that were being refilled illegally. The District Supply Officer said that domestic cylinders were being refilled using commercial cylinders. Inspection teams are conducting checks in different parts of the city to prevent such illegal activities. Authorities are monitoring the situation closely to ensure that gas cylinders are distributed legally and reach genuine consumers. Hotels and restaurants affected in several cities The disruption in gas supply has started affecting the hospitality sector in cities such as Jaipur and Jodhpur. Due to the shortage of cylinders, many hotels and restaurants have begun to suspend their operations. Several large restaurants have reduced their menus by nearly half to manage the limited gas supply. Restaurant operators claim that gas agencies are charging arbitrary prices for cylinders. At the same time, domestic consumers are also facing difficulties. Due to the shortage of household gas cylinders, long queues are being seen outside gas agencies. Special monitoring teams formed The Food Supply Department has issued instructions to District Supply Officers in every district to form special inspection teams. These teams will include local enforcement officers from the supply department as well as officials from the police and district administration. The teams will closely monitor the supply of both domestic and commercial cylinders. The central government has also instructed that gas supply must continue on a priority basis to essential sectors. These priority sectors include educational institutions, hospitals and other essential service organisations. Each inspection team has been directed to conduct random checks of at least two gas agencies every week. During these inspections, officials will examine stock records and verify supply details. They will review how many cylinders are supplied daily by gas companies to each agency and where those cylinders are distributed. The aim is to prevent black marketing in the market and ensure timely supply to ordinary consumers. If any irregularities are found in an agency’s records or if excessive stock is discovered, strict action will be taken against the agency. Action possible against agencies over complaints The Food Department has also instructed its teams to take action against agencies if complaints are received regarding the supply of gas cylinders to institutions or ordinary consumers. The department’s secretary has directed District Supply Officers to carry out special monitoring to ensure uninterrupted supply of gas to priority sectors. Demand for wood and coal furnaces rises in Kota The shortage of gas cylinders has also led to an increased demand for traditional wood and coal furnaces in Kota. Artisans who manufacture these furnaces are receiving a large number of orders. A shopkeeper named Jabbar said that around 45 furnaces have been prepared in the past two days alone, and more than 40 additional orders have already been received. Furnaces weighing between 35 and 40 kilograms are being made especially for mess facilities and hostels. However, due to the sharp rise in demand, craftsmen say it has become difficult to meet the supply requirements.

stories.title: Mathura businessman claims Ashutosh Maharaj did not pay for Scorpio:Says, FIR was filed against him instead; alleges the trust is fake
stories.summary: Ashutosh Brahmachari, who recently filed a sexual abuse case against Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand involving two young disciples, continues to remain in the news. Now, a property dealer from Mathura, Manish Chaturvedi, has levelled fresh allegations against him. Manish claims that Ashutosh Brahmachari purchased a Mahindra Scorpio from him in 2023 but paid only a small portion of the agreed amount. According to him, the total deal was worth ₹18 lakh, but he received only ₹2.5 lakh. After that, Ashutosh allegedly filed an FIR against him. Manish also said that he lodged a complaint against Ashutosh in return. According to him, the police visited Ashutosh’s residence six times to recover the Scorpio but were unsuccessful. He further alleged that the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Nirman Trust, which Ashutosh claims to head as president, is also fake. Responding to these allegations, Ashutosh Brahmachari admitted that he bought the Scorpio from Manish but said the agreed price was ₹13.5 lakh. He claimed he had already paid ₹13 lakh and only ₹50,000 remained pending. According to him, Manish later began demanding an additional ₹5 lakh. Ashutosh also stated that the High Court has granted him a stay on the FIR filed against him. How did the dispute began ? Property dealer purchased the vehicle in 2023 The dispute revolves around a Mahindra Scorpio Classic (S11) that Ashutosh Brahmachari uses for travel. The vehicle was originally purchased by Mathura-based property dealer Manish Chaturvedi. Manish bought the Scorpio on 17 January 2023 for around ₹19 lakh. His business partner, Dhananjay Bhardwaj, was also associated with the vehicle and both used it regularly. Deal finalised for ₹18 Lakh Manish said he initially did not know Ashutosh Brahmachari personally. According to him, their associate Dhananjay Bhardwaj was connected with organisations such as Bhagwa Dal and knew Ashutosh. Dhananjay reportedly suggested selling the vehicle to Ashutosh, describing him as a trustworthy person. Acting on this suggestion, Manish agreed to the deal. By then, the car had run approximately 20,000 kilometres in about 11 months. On 23 December 2023, a deal for ₹18 lakh was finalised and a written agreement was prepared between both parties. Allegation: Only partial payment made Manish claims that after handing over the vehicle, Ashutosh made payments of about ₹2.25 lakh in instalments over seven days through online transactions. After that, no further payment was made. He said he repeatedly asked for the remaining amount but did not receive it. Eventually, on 2 May 2025, he filed an FIR at Govindnagar police station in Mathura and submitted all the documents related to the vehicle. Manish said he even told the police that if they recovered the car, he would return the money already received What the police investigation found ? According to the police investigation, the Scorpio remained registered in the name of Manish Chaturvedi. Manish also provided bank statements showing the payments he had received from Ashutosh. Police summoned Ashutosh Brahmachari to the station, but he allegedly did not appear. Manish claims the biggest challenge for the police was recovering the vehicle. Police reportedly visited Ashutosh’s residence in Raizadgan, Kandhla, six times to recover the Scorpio but returned empty-handed each time. Ashutosh later approached the High Court against the Govindnagar police station SHO. The court stayed his arrest but did not halt the recovery of the vehicle. When the police failed to recover the vehicle, they filed a charge sheet. Manish then approached the High Court again, which ordered a reinvestigation and directed that the vehicle be recovered. According to Manish, three different inspectors have handled the case so far, but the Scorpio has still not been recovered. Counter case filed by Ashutosh Brahmachari Meanwhile, Ashutosh Brahmachari filed a case against Manish Chaturvedi in the Kairana Court. In that case, an agreement dated 22 March 2024 was presented, stating that the deal for the vehicle had been finalised at ₹13.5 lakh and the payment had been completed. Manish alleges that the documents submitted in court are forged. He claims that the signature shown as his in the agreement is not genuine. He also stated that he has never visited the court where the petition was filed and had not received any notice regarding the case. Claim of police suggesting a ‘Thief’ Manish also shared an audio recording of a conversation with a policeman with Dainik Bhaskar. In the recording, the policeman allegedly says that a “thief” could recover the vehicle within ten days and asked Manish to cooperate. Manish claims the discussion was about stealing back the car. When asked why the police would suggest such a step, he said Ashutosh is a powerful person and that officials are afraid of him. However, Manish said he refused to take such help. In a response submitted during a public hearing on 26 November 2024, Sub-Inspector Narendra Singh Tomar of Govindnagar police station stated that several raids had been conducted to arrest Ashutosh but he was not cooperating with the investigation. The report also said Ashutosh had not recorded his statement and that a non-bailable warrant had been issued by the court. It also described him as a history-sheeter at Kandhla police station with record number 76A. Allegations regarding the trust Manish has also questioned the authenticity of the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Nirman Trust, which Ashutosh claims to lead. According to him, when they investigated the trust, they discovered that the address listed for it had no connection with any such organisation. He alleged that the trust was registered at the residence of a man named Rajul Sharma. When contacted, Rajul Sharma confirmed that on 6 December 2024, they received a police notice about the trust being registered at their home address. He said they were surprised because no such organisation operated there. Sharma said he had met Ashutosh once at a meeting where he was offered a position as president of the trust in Mathura but declined. He added that they later wrote to the Local Intelligence Unit requesting the removal of the trust registration from their address. Ashutosh Brahmachari’s response Responding to the allegations, Ashutosh Brahmachari maintained that the Scorpio deal was worth ₹13.5 lakh. He said ₹13 lakh had already been paid and the remaining ₹50,000 was to be given when the vehicle was transferred to his name. According to him, Manish later demanded an additional ₹5 lakh, which led to the dispute and the FIR. Ashutosh acknowledged that the police visited his residence several times, but said he would respond only after receiving proper information from them. He also stated that he obtained a stay order from the High Court against punitive action in the case. When asked about the court’s direction regarding recovery of the vehicle, Ashutosh reportedly said the police could come and take it if they had the authority. He further alleged that on 12 April 2025, Manish and his brother came to Vrindavan to forcibly take the vehicle. According to him, they entered his ashram, abused and assaulted him and his followers. Ashutosh said he filed a case against them in response, after which both brothers were sent to jail and a charge sheet was filed in that case as well.

stories.title: Woman strangles mother-in-law to death in Mathura:Tells husband she suffered sudden attack; truth exposed during fight with sister-in-law
stories.summary: Police on Wednesday revealed the murder of an elderly woman in Mathura. The crime was carried out by her daughter-in-law along with her lover. The two allegedly strangled the woman to death and then fabricated a story of a silent attack in front of family members. Believing their version, the family buried the elderly woman. Later, during an argument at home, the daughter-in-law accidentally revealed the truth when she threatened her sister-in-law, saying, ‘Just like I killed your mother, I will finish you too.’ After hearing this, the family approached the police. The police then exhumed the body from the grave and conducted a post-mortem. The post-mortem revealed that the woman had been strangled, causing her neck bone to break. After this, police arrested the accused daughter-in-law and her lover, who is her paternal brother-in-law. Both were presented in court and sent to jail. The case is from the Raya police station area. See 2 photos Full incident details Daughter-in-law, lover confess elderly woman's murder On March 11, police arrested Hina. During interrogation, she told police that she had a love affair with Adil, a boy from the neighborhood, and that both of them carried out the murder together. Hina revealed that she and Adil had been in a relationship for the past two years. Her husband and father-in-law were often away from home, leaving only her elderly mother-in-law, Anwari, in the house. Whenever Anwari was not home or was asleep, Adil used to visit her. On the night of March 2, Adil had come to meet her. Late at night, Anwari woke up and saw them in a compromising position. Fearing their secret would be exposed, Hina and Adil conspired to eliminate her. They caught Anwari and strangled her to death. After the murder, Adil returned to his home, while Hina called her husband Aamir in Noida and told him that Anwari had died due to a silent attack. Aamir's marriage took place 6 years ago Amir's marriage (nikah) to Hina, a resident of Kota Kapura village in Hathras, took place in 2020. Amir often stayed out with his father for work. During this time, Hina had an affair with Adil, her uncle's son, who lived in the neighborhood. Adil lives in the village and farms.

stories.title: Suspended IAS officer reinstated in ₹1 crore bribery case:Yogi govt had suspended Abhishek Prakash a year ago after businessman’s complaint
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has reinstated suspended IAS officer Abhishek Prakash after nearly a year. He had earlier been accused of demanding a commission of ₹1 crore from businessman Vishwajeet Dutta through his close aide, Babu Nikant Jain, in exchange for approving a solar industry project. When the payment was allegedly not made, the project file was reportedly stalled. The businessman later lodged a complaint with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Acting on the complaint, the Chief Minister ordered an investigation by the Special Task Force (STF). During the probe, the STF arrested Babu Nikant Jain, who reportedly admitted that he had demanded the bribe at the behest of Abhishek Prakash. However, Jain later challenged his arrest by filing a petition in the Lucknow High Court. Complainant retracts statement in court On February 10 this year, businessman Vishwajeet Dutta withdrew his earlier statement before the Lucknow High Court. He said the complaint had been filed due to a misunderstanding. Following this statement, the court dismissed the case. Since then, speculation about Abhishek Prakash’s reinstatement had been growing. According to sources, the officer is considered close to two influential IAS officers in Uttar Pradesh—one retired and the other currently serving, which may help him secure an important posting soon. Businessman had complained directly to CM Yogi The controversy began last year when investor Vishwajeet Dutta approached Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath with a complaint. Dutta said that his company, SEAL Solar P6 Private Limited, wanted to establish a manufacturing unit in Uttar Pradesh for producing solar cells and related components. He had submitted an application through the Invest UP office as well as online. During the evaluation process, the application was discussed in a committee meeting. According to Dutta, a senior IAS officer gave him the phone number of Nikant Jain and advised him to speak with him, saying the project file would be approved quickly if Jain recommended it. When Dutta contacted Jain, he allegedly demanded a 5 per cent commission, around ₹1 crore. When Dutta refused to pay, Jain reportedly told him that the project would not move forward without the payment. Clerk admitted to demanding bribe Following the complaint, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed the STF to investigate the matter. On March 20, 2025, the STF arrested Nikant Jain, a clerk associated with the case. A case was registered against him at the Gomti Nagar police station in Lucknow. During interrogation, Jain admitted that he had demanded a commission. After the arrest, IAS officer Abhishek Prakash was suspended from service. At that time, he was serving as Secretary of the Industrial Development Department and Chief Executive Officer of Invest UP. Since the suspension, he had largely remained out of public view. Previous allegations against Abhishek Prakash Abhishek Prakash has faced several allegations during his administrative career- 1. Defence Corridor land case Questions were raised about his role in land acquisition for the Defence Corridor project in Bhatgaon, Lucknow. As chairman of the land acquisition committee, he was accused of arbitrarily fixing land rates in coordination with local revenue officials. Land originally allotted to Scheduled Caste beneficiaries in 1984 was allegedly made saleable, leading to claims of compensation worth ₹20 crore through collusion between brokers and officials. 2. Irregularities during tenure as LDA Vice Chairman While serving as Vice Chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA), he faced accusations of favouring certain builders. Sources claimed that although he ordered demolitions of illegal constructions, he allegedly benefited builders close to him. Licences were reportedly issued to preferred developers in several areas, including Ashiana, and there were also allegations that builders’ files were deliberately delayed through collusion with officials. 3. Complaints during District postings Prakash has also served as District Magistrate in Aligarh, Lakhimpur Kheri and Hamirpur. During these tenures, complaints emerged regarding irregularities in land transactions in Aligarh, alleged manipulation in government tenders in Lakhimpur, and suspected links with mining mafias in Hamirpur. 4. Allegations of large land purchases He has also been accused of purchasing around 700 bighas of land in Lakhimpur Kheri and Bareilly in the names of family members, including his parents and brother, as well as through several companies. Additionally, he allegedly acquired around 400 bighas in Bareilly. Authorities have also raised concerns about possible stamp duty evasion in these transactions.

stories.title: Black marketing of LPG cylinders begins in Lucknow:Being sold for ₹1,600–₹3,500 ; hotels restaurants start shutting down
stories.summary: The shortage of LPG gas cylinders in Lucknow is continuously increasing. Due to the disrupted supply of both domestic and commercial cylinders, people associated with the hotel, restaurant and catering businesses are facing serious difficulties, and their work has started getting affected. At the same time, common consumers are also struggling. Earlier, cylinders were usually delivered the very next day after booking, but now many households are not receiving cylinders even after a week. Because of this, the waiting period for domestic cylinders is increasing rapidly. Hotel operators, traders, shopkeepers and ordinary residents across the city are facing problems due to the shortage. Several people shared their experiences about how the crisis is affecting daily life. Hotels on the verge of shutting down Jitendra, Financial Controller of Piccadilly Hotel, said that earlier, there was no information about any shortage of gas cylinders. However, suddenly, news about the shortage started spreading, and the situation deteriorated quickly. According to him, the supplier has now refused to provide cylinders from Wednesday. Once the existing gas cylinders finished, the hotel faced immediate operational problems. Jitendra said the situation in the market has become very difficult. Even commercial induction cooktops, which could have been used as an alternative, are currently not available in the market. Some people are thinking of using coal for cooking, but that option is neither easy nor practical for large kitchens. He said the government should take the issue seriously because the shortage has created confusion across the city. According to him, the situation is slowly moving toward panic if the supply is not restored soon. Gas finished at the agency, cylinder sold for Rs 1600 in black Rinku Chaurasia, who came from Buddheshwar to Lalbagh to refill his cylinder, said there has been no gas in his house for the past four days. His family has five members and all of them are forced to eat meals at their neighbors’ houses. He said he has been visiting the gas agency continuously for four days but has not been able to get a cylinder anywhere. Gas is not available at the agency, but the same cylinder is easily available in the black market for Rs 1600. Normally the cylinder costs around Rs 950, but now it is being sold at almost double the price. According to Rinku, there is open black market of cylinders in the city. He added that not only gas cylinders, but prices of essential items like potatoes, onions and tomatoes have also increased. The situation, he said, reminds people of the COVID period when oxygen cylinders were sold in the black market. Now LPG cylinders are being sold the same way. Rinku also said that a large number of people are standing in queues outside agencies, but there is no one to address their concerns. According to him, an issue occurring elsewhere is affecting ordinary people here, and cylinders are becoming expensive. Leaving work and business to stand in queues Vinay Maurya, who came from Jankipuram to refill his cylinder, said he had travelled around 22 kilometers to reach the agency. He had been standing in line for the last five hours, but still could not get a cylinder. According to Vinay, people received information that the gas truck arrived only after about a week, which is why the queue became extremely long. He said that in the past 10 years, he had never had to stand in such a long line just to get a gas cylinder. Vinay said that due to the shortage, breakfast at his home had to be cooked on a wood stove in the morning. Only after getting a cylinder will normal cooking resume in the household. Cylinder not available since March 5 Another consumer, Manisha, said standing in line for a gas cylinder has become very frustrating. She said her family has been trying to get a cylinder since March 5 but has not succeeded. According to her, online booking is also not working, and people are forced to visit gas agencies repeatedly. Agency staff are saying that gas will be available only after the DAC number is generated, but the online DAC number is not being issued. Meanwhile, the same cylinder is available in the black market for around Rs 1500. She alleged that people are being deliberately made to stand in lines so that cylinders can be sold at higher prices. Manisha said people have left their homes and families to stand in queues. Many parents have even brought their small children along, and some children have skipped school while waiting at agencies with gas cylinders. Ramadan becomes difficult without cylinders Mohammed Sharif, who came to collect a cylinder, said the shortage has created serious problems during the month of Ramadan. People are forced to stand in lines for hours, yet the agency staff do not provide clear information. According to Sharif, all members of his family are observing fasts at home. However, there has been no gas cylinder in the house for the past two days. Because of this, the family has been forced to buy food items for Iftar and meals from outside markets. He said the situation is troubling especially for children. Sharif added that if gas cylinders are supplied on time, a major problem for many families can be resolved. Stood in line three times but still no cylinder Aryan, another consumer, said he had been standing in line at the agency for about six hours but still did not receive gas. When his turn finally came, agency employees asked him to bring the gas passbook. After bringing the passbook, he had to stand in line again. Later, the employees asked him to bring the mobile phone through which the booking had been made. Aryan said he stood in line for the third time with the phone, but even then, he could not get the cylinder. He alleged that agency employees do not explain the entire process properly at once, which creates more confusion and trouble for consumers. Aryan said his family members are waiting for gas at home while he has been struggling in the queue for hours. Situation reaches the point of closing kitchens Lalit Mehta, owner of Mehta Sweets, said gas cylinders are the most essential requirement for their business. Until the Holi festival, they had no idea that such a problem could arise. However, as soon as the Holi celebrations ended, the shortage started affecting businesses. On Wednesday morning, work in the shop’s kitchen had almost come to a halt. He said the gas agency and delivery personnel are not answering calls, which has created confusion among business owners. According to Lalit, all the stock prepared for Holi has already been sold, and they are unable to make new items due to the lack of gas. Each passing day is making the situation more difficult. Small shopkeepers and tea vendors have already started shutting their shops because of the shortage, and business owners say they do not know how long they will be able to continue operations if the supply does not improve.

stories.title: Fog-like conditions in eastern UP, visibility drops to 30 metres:Mist seen in March after 18 years; weather may worsen in two days
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh changed suddenly on Thursday, with fog-like conditions reported in several districts of Purvanchal, including Mau, Gorakhpur and Ballia. A layer of mist has been present since morning, significantly reducing visibility. In Mau, visibility dropped to around 30 metres, while in several cities including Bareilly, it ranged between 100 and 500 metres. Fog seen in March after 18 years According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), such foggy conditions in March have appeared in the state after nearly 18 years. Weather conditions are expected to deteriorate further from March 15, with the possibility of rain in some areas accompanied by strong winds. Heat also intensifying in the state At the same time, temperatures have started rising sharply across the state. Banda was recorded as the hottest city, with the maximum temperature reaching 38.6°C. The temperature also crossed 36°C in Agra, Jhansi, Maharajganj and Hamirpur. Fog triggers road accidents Due to poor visibility on Wednesday, nine vehicles were involved in four separate road accidents across the state. Three people died and around 30 others were injured in these incidents. Western disturbance likely to affect weather Atul Kumar Singh, senior scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, said the fog was caused by moisture-laden winds and dust particles trapped in the air. He added that a western disturbance is likely to become active from March 14, which could bring light to moderate rainfall in the Terai and Purvanchal regions on March 15 and 16. See the pictures of fog- In March 2008 also, the state had such foggy weather Atul Kumar Singh said - Similar foggy conditions had also occurred in March 2008. This is a normal seasonal phenomenon. Due to global warming, these fluctuations in temperature could become a major challenge for agriculture, health and environment in the future. Although the fog has cleared with the rising sun, it has left behind many deep questions about climate protection. Avoid going out in strong sunlight Doctors have advised people to avoid going out in strong sunlight during afternoon hours and drink adequate water. The weather could have mixed effects for farmers. While light rain could prove beneficial for crops, there are concerns about damage to standing crops from intense heat and winds. How will the weather be for next 3 days Another sudden reason for fog? Banaras Hindu University (BHU) meteorologist Manoj Srivastava said - a low-pressure system has formed between Bihar and Marathwada. Due to this, foggy conditions are developing in some parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh during morning hours. Wind is blowing close to the surface. Therefore, a slight drop in temperature has been observed, but temperature will increase as the day progresses. He said - due to the upcoming active western disturbance, temperatures across the state will gradually decrease from March 14. From March 15, light rain will occur for the first time this season in the Terai regions along with some parts of Purvanchal. This spell will continue for a few days. Later, temperatures will start rising. Why is the heat increasing in March? Skymet Weather's Vice President Mahesh Palawat says that in recent years, the effect of climate change is clearly visible on the weather. Due to this, the weather pattern is changing rapidly. Summer is starting earlier compared to before. The effect is that now the temperature is rising more rapidly. The number of hot days is also increasing. Sometimes the heat wave period also lasts longer than before. In the past few years, old heat records have been broken in many cities across the country. In some places, temperatures have been recorded above 48 degrees. Heatwave could last for a long time According to IMD's forecast, heatwave conditions may persist for a long time in some areas this year. This means that temperatures could remain very high for several consecutive days in many cities and people may have to face intense heat. When is it considered a heatwave? According to the Meteorological Department, a heatwave is declared when the temperature in plains reaches 40 degrees Celsius or higher, or when the temperature recorded is 4 to 6 degrees above normal. In such conditions, people's health can be affected and the risk of heat stroke increases. Heat will damage crops

stories.title: 9-year old falls through broken school bus floor, dies:Wheel runs over child; family alleges bus hidden in Agra
stories.summary: A 9-year-old student died after falling from a moving school bus in Agra on Wednesday. The bus wheel ran over her after she fell. When other children raised an alarm, the driver stopped the vehicle. The girl was rushed to a hospital but doctors declared her dead. The victim, Naina, was a Class 1 student. The accident occurred near Biharipura in the Etmadpur police station area. Bus in poor condition, children seated on wooden planks According to the family, the school bus was in a dilapidated condition. Instead of proper seats, children were made to sit on wooden planks placed over broken sections of the floor. It is alleged that the driver did not slow down at a speed breaker. The bus crossed it with a strong jolt, causing one of the planks to slip. Naina lost balance and fell from the moving bus, after which the bus wheel ran over her. She was taken to a private hospital, where doctors declared her dead. See 2 pictures... Naina travelled to school with her elder sister Naina, daughter of Brahmajeet from Nagla Lale village, studied at RBS School in Bhagupur. Her elder sister Pari, a Class 5 student, also studied at the same school. Family members said the two sisters left for school together by the bus as usual. They were returning home after school ended around 3 PM when the accident occurred. Family alleges school did not inform them Naina’s father Brahmajeet alleged that the school management did not immediately inform the family about the incident. He said that when he contacted the school, he was told that the child had met with an accident and had been admitted to Goyal Hospital. “By the time we reached the hospital, our daughter had already died,” he said. Mother and grandmother faint in hospital The news of Naina’s death left the family devastated. Her grandmother Pancho Devi and mother Sonam fainted in the hospital while crying. The grieving grandmother repeatedly said: “This morning Naina told me she would play with me after returning from school. Please bring my daughter back.” Sister rushed home with the news Naina’s uncle Yogesh said the girl died because the bus floor was broken, causing her to fall. He said Naina’s sister Pari rushed home and informed the family about the accident. When they contacted the school, they were told about the incident. By the time the family reached the hospital, the child had died. Police register FIR Etmadpur Station House Officer Alok Kumar said police received information about the girl's death in the accident. “The family has filed a complaint. The body has been sent for post-mortem. An FIR has been registered and further action is underway,” he said. A similar accident happened in Aligarh on March 1 School bus floor broke while moving, girl fell down In Aligarh on March 1, a student died after being crushed by a school bus. The student was returning home with her brother in the school bus. During this time, the iron sheet of the bus floor broke and the student fell down. She came under the wheel. The student's brother shouted - Uncle, stop the bus, sister has fallen down. When the driver stopped and looked, the girl had died. After this, the driver threatened her brother not to tell anyone about the incident. After the accident, the driver informed the student's family about her injury. Then he laid the student on the back seat and started running away. As soon as villagers saw the bus driver fleeing, they chased and caught him after about 2 km. After this, the villagers created a ruckus and blocked the road.

stories.title: UP woman’s IAS claim turns fake:Celebrated securing 113th rank in UPSC 2025; probe reveals she didn’t even qualify mains
stories.summary: After Bihar’s Akanksha, a similar case has surfaced in Uttar Pradesh where Shikha Gautam’s claim of becoming an IAS officer in the UPSC-2025 results has turned out to be false. When the results were announced on March 6, Shikha Gautam claimed she had secured 113th rank. At the same time, another woman named Shikha from Delhi also claimed the same rank. The Delhi-based Shikha later emailed UPSC requesting clarification. Following this, the commission asked the Bulandshahr District Magistrate Shruti to conduct an inquiry. Tehsildar sent to verify documents DM Shruti directed the ADM (Administration) to get the matter investigated through SDM Sadar Dinesh Chandra and submit a report. The SDM then sent Sadar Tehsildar Manoj Rawat to Shikha Gautam’s house to verify the documents. During the verification, the Tehsildar found that Shikha Gautam’s claim was false. According to officials, Shikha Gautam had not even cleared the UPSC Main examination, and therefore she was not shortlisted for the interview stage. In her documents, her name was also recorded as Shikha Rani. Family believed the claim, celebrations held Shikha had kept her family unaware of the reality. After the results were declared, she told them that she had been selected in UPSC. Her grandfather reportedly broke down in happiness, and the family as well as villagers celebrated the news with drums and music. Later, the SDM said Shikha Gautam and her family have admitted their mistake. However, UPSC has not yet issued an official clarification on whether the Delhi-based Shikha is the candidate who actually secured 113th rank. See 3 photos... Delhi’s Shikha currently posted as BDPO Meanwhile, the Delhi-based Shikha, who claims the 113th rank, is currently posted as Block Development and Panchayat Officer (BDPO) in Sampla, Rohtak district. Speaking to The Tribune, she said she was shocked after seeing a video on social media claiming that a Shikha from Bulandshahr had secured the 113th rank. She said the name appearing at 113th rank in the UPSC merit list is hers, and the roll number also belongs to her. After noticing the confusion, she emailed UPSC seeking clarification. Shikha has completed her Bachelor’s (Honours) degree in Economics from Delhi. She further said that she had earlier secured 7th rank in the Combined Defence Services (CDS) exam, but did not join because she was selected in the Haryana Civil Service in the same year. She joined the Haryana government in May 2025 and has been posted in Sampla since July 2025. There was also a dispute over UPSC rank-301 UP's Akanksha is real, Bihar's Brahmeshwar Mukhia's granddaughter's claim is fake, roll number was same 2 days ago, UPSC issued a clarification regarding the claims of 2 Akanksha Singh for rank-301 in the final result. The commission issued a letter stating - rank-301 belongs to Akanksha Singh from Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh. Her father's name is Ranjit Singh and mother's name is Neelam Singh. The roll number is 0856794. Akanksha from UP-Bihar had claimed 301st rank... The Civil Services Examination 2025 final result was declared on March 6. After the result was released, two candidates with the same name, Akanksha Singh, claimed to have secured rank 301 in the final merit list. Claims emerged from two different Akanksha Singhs from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar regarding the 301st rank. Actually, in the merit list released by UPSC, Akanksha Singh's name is registered at AIR 301, with roll number 0856794. This led to confusion after both candidates made their claims. There was a discrepancy in Bihar's Akanksha's admit card Bhaskar checked the admit cards of both candidates to investigate the matter. The interview call letter of Akanksha from Ghazipur, UP shows roll number 0856794. The same roll number was visible when scanning the QR code on this admit card. Meanwhile, Akanksha Singh from Ara, Bihar provided her prelims admit card to Bhaskar. This also showed roll number 0856794, but when scanning the QR code, roll number 085659 was visible. Challenge given to Bihar's Akanksha... Akanksha from Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh told Dainik Bhaskar that she appeared for Mains in August 2025 and interview on February 4, 2026 with roll number 0856794. She said - "I am clear that this result is mine, you can verify from the code or roll number on my admit card. There is no doubt on UPSC's site. There has been misinformation in the media. The entire matter is clear that this result is mine." If Akanksha from Ara thinks the result is hers, she should come forward and refute this with proof. I don't know on what basis Akanksha from Ara has seen the result. I appeared for all three tests including Mains with this same roll number. My father helps me appear for every exam. When I filled the form, I received this roll number. Bihar's Akanksha said - This is UPSC's mistake Akanksha from Bihar belongs to Khopira village of Agiyanw block in Bhojpur district. However, her family lives in Ara city. In conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Akanksha admitted her mistake. She said, “My roll number is 0856569 only, now this discrepancy is not mine but UPSC's.”

stories.title: Lucknow celebrates India’s T20 World Cup victory on streets:Fans gather with tricolours, burst firecrackers and dance in Hazratganj
stories.summary: Celebrations have broken out across Lucknow following India’s victory in the T20 World Cup. People have gathered at major intersections carrying the national tricolour and distributing sweets. Firecrackers are being burst and coloured powder is being thrown in the air. Amid the celebrations, the Hazratganj area has become completely congested. Even before the match ended, people had begun dancing to ‘bhangra’ in areas such as Kapurthala and Hazratganj. CM Yogi Adityanath also posted on X and congratulated the Indian Cricket Team Large screens installed across the city In several parts of the city, arrangements had been made for residents to watch the match together. Large screens and projectors were installed at multiple locations. LED screens were set up in markets, while parks hosted tented viewing areas where people watched the match on projectors. Big screens were placed at Rajajipuram, Madiyanv and Kapurthala intersections. In Gomti Nagar’s Vinamra Khand park, residents gathered to watch the match collectively. In the Ismailganj Second Ward area, the World Cup final was screened on a large display at Dayal Park alongside a Holi Milan celebration. Match screened at social gatherings At Annapurna Ground in Nigohan, a tilak ceremony also featured an LED screen where guests and invitees watched the match together. Earlier in the day, a marathon in support of Team India was organised at the 1090 intersection by the Lucknow Super Giants franchise. Later, a havan was performed in Gomti Nagar with prayers for India’s victory. Due to the large number of fans gathering in central areas, the police are struggling to manage traffic. The presence of cricket supporters has caused traffic to come to a halt in Hazratganj. See 7 pictures of the celebration-

He wasn't given it because he is PDA. Akhilesh Yadav reached the home of social worker Mewalal in Jankipuram, Lucknow, on Sunday. Mewalal's son is getting married this evening. It was here that when journalists asked a question related to the President's protocol in Bengal, Akhilesh Yadav targeted the BJP. He said- BJP will find fault with anything, one should be very careful with them. One should be very careful with conspiracies and plots. How much do they follow protocol? They should tell how much protocol they follow? How much respect do they give to others? What Akhilesh saidin 3 points What did the SP chief say yesterday? Akhilesh Yadav had said on Saturday that Keshav Maurya should remain healthy. Such an incident should not happen to anyone. Because, it's a machine and we all fly in that machine. We all travel. The machine should always be good.

stories.title: CM Yogi attends 'Pink Rozgar Mahakumbh' event in Lucknow:Announces free scooties for girl students, employment will be given to 5,000 women
stories.summary: During the ‘Pink Rozgar Mahakumbh’ event in Lucknow, Minister Pratibha Shukla sang a song on stage. Listening to the performance, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath responded with humour and said that when Pratibha Shukla was singing, he was thinking it was good that she was singing now, otherwise Lata Mangeshkar might have taken retirement. After remarking, Yogi burst into laughter and said that the title of Swar Samragni should actually have been given to her. He then added that it was still a good effort. He said that when someone overcomes hesitation and speaks or performs publicly, it reflects their confidence. Women’s Day programme at IGP In fact, Yogi was speaking at a programme organised on the occasion of Women’s Day at IGP. During the event, he distributed cheques to girls under the Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana. He also interacted warmly with beneficiaries. He affectionately handed a teddy bear to a young girl who had accompanied one of the beneficiaries and also gave her chocolates. The Chief Minister spoke with young women present at the programme and encouraged one of them by saying, ‘Study well and become successful.’ Announcement of free scooties for students Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister announced that the government would soon provide free scooties to girl students. The benefit will be given to students in the final year of graduation and post-graduation. He said that daughters would no longer have to depend on anyone, and the government would support them in both education and employment. Employment and initiatives under Pink Mahakumbh 2026 Under Pink Mahakumbh 2026, there is a plan to provide employment opportunities to 5,000 women. The event will also witness the launch of the Sangam portal mobile application, distribution of appointment letters to 94 newly appointed mukhya sevikas, and the presentation of Nari Shakti Awards. Additionally, Anganwadi workers will receive ₹3,849 lakh directly in their bank accounts through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system. See 4 pictures-

stories.title: Mayawati targets Mamata over President Murmu visit controversy:Calls protocol breach unfortunate; asks parties to respect constitutional posts
stories.summary: Mayawati on Sunday criticised the alleged protocol breach during the recent West Bengal visit of Droupadi Murmu and said constitutional posts should never be politicised. In a post on X, the BSP supremo said everyone should respect the dignity and protocol attached to the office of the President as per the ideals of the Indian Constitution. She said the current President is not only a woman but also belongs to the tribal community, and the events during her recent visit to West Bengal were “extremely unfortunate”. Mayawati’s remarks came amid a political controversy over the absence of senior state representatives during Murmu’s visit to North Bengal. Mayawati also raises issue of Lok Sabha Speaker’s dignity Mayawati also criticised the opposition’s behaviour in Parliament towards the Om Birla. She said the politicisation of the Speaker’s position in Parliament in recent times was not appropriate and urged all parties to rise above political differences and maintain the dignity of constitutional posts. The BSP chief also appealed for the smooth functioning of Parliament in the interest of the country and public welfare. The second phase of the Budget Session of Parliament will begin on March 9. What happened during President Murmu’s West Bengal visit? President Murmu had arrived in North Bengal near Siliguri on March 7 to attend the 9th International Santhal Conference. The venue of the event was reportedly changed at the last moment from Bidhannagar to Gosaipur. The size of the venue was also smaller, due to which many members of the tribal community could not attend the programme. Another issue that sparked controversy was the absence of senior leaders from the state government to receive the President. Traditionally, the Chief Minister of a state welcomes the President during official visits. In the Chief Minister’s absence, the senior-most minister usually receives the President. However, neither West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee nor any state minister was present to receive Murmu. During the programme, the President expressed displeasure over the matter. She said that as per protocol, the Chief Minister or a minister from the state government should have been present to receive her. Murmu added that she personally had no objection but said such traditions should be followed to maintain dignity and protocol. PM Modi says President’s office is above politics Narendra Modi also commented on the controversy on X. He said people who believe in strengthening democracy and the tribal community were saddened by the incident. Modi added that the office of the President is above politics and its dignity should always be maintained. He also expressed hope that the West Bengal government and the Trinamool Congress would reflect on the matter. Mamata Banerjee hits back at criticism Responding to the controversy, Mamata Banerjee said criticism of West Bengal was politically motivated. She said before commenting on West Bengal, the President should first look at the situation in states ruled by the BJP. Speaking at a protest site in Kolkata, Banerjee alleged that the BJP was trying to defame West Bengal by using President Murmu. She also said the information given to the President about the absence of state representatives at the event was incorrect.

stories.title: Father kills 2 children, hangs himself:In Maharajganj he wrote on wall wife and her lover responsible; woman works in armed forces
stories.summary: In Maharajganj, the husband of a female Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel killed his innocent son and daughter before committing suicide. He hung both children from the window using a rope. Then he committed suicide by hanging himself from the roof hook. Before dying, the husband wrote a suicide note on the room wall - 'The cause of our death is my wife and her lover Sonu Gautam. Even while living with me, she talks to Sonu. I cannot separate the children from myself.' The incident occurred at 7 AM on Sunday. When the husband killed the children, they screamed. Hearing this, tenants living on the lower floor became suspicious. They called out but got no response. They came up to check. They knocked on the door but it didn't open. Then they called the female personnel. She was on duty at that time. The female personnel came home after a while. She knocked on the door, but it didn't open. After breaking down the door, everyone was shocked to see inside. The bodies of the 4-year-old son and 3-year-old daughter were hanging by the window. Meanwhile, the husband's body was hanging in the room. Police and SSB jawans also reached the spot. Due to duty at the Nepal border in Nautanwa, the female jawan lived on rent with her family in the Gandhi Nagar area. Her husband stayed at home and did not do any work. The family originally belongs to Saidpur in Ghazipur. See three pictures Tenant heard screaming Vandana Bharti (35) is posted in the fourth class at the 66th Battalion SSB in Nautanwa. She married Amresh (40) in 2019. She has been working since before marriage. She came here a year ago, before that she was posted in Jharkhand. Vandana lived on the first floor of a rented house here with her husband, son Amarendra Kumar (4) and daughter Kanchan (3). On Saturday evening, Vandana went on duty. Then she came early Sunday morning and after finishing her work, went back on duty. Around 7 am, the tenant living downstairs in the house heard screaming. When he went upstairs, Vandana's room gate was locked from inside. After this, he called Vandana. Children found hanging from window and husband from fan hook Vandana left her duty and came to the room. When she broke down the door and entered, she was shocked by the scene. She fainted upon seeing the bodies of her son, daughter and husband. Vandana's entire family was gone. When she regained consciousness after a while, she lay on the floor crying and flailing her arms and legs. She fainted again while crying and holding onto the bodies of the innocents. Amaresh wrote a suicide note on the wall- Even while staying with me, Vandana calls Sonu. She says you can't do anything to me. I can't keep my children away. The cause of our death is my wife Vandana Kumari (SSB) and her lover Sonu Gautam, Vandana's father Ram Avatar, mother Chanda Devi, brother Naveen Kumar, his wife Sunita Devi and Amarnath. These people call my wife to their home for money. Wife gives 5000 rupees every month. Her lover Sonu Gautam also takes this money. Because of Sonu, the entire family is destroyed today. Before suicide, Amrish made a video and sent it to his brother-in-law, read what he said? My wife should not touch my body, she has ruined me I, Amrish Thakur, am issuing this statement in full consciousness. The cause of our death is none other than my wife and her family members. My wife is Vandana Kumari (SSB 66th Battalion). My wife often says that she will take me to the camp and have me beaten with sticks and will also have my family members picked up. She used to say give me a divorce, or I will ruin you. We have two children, so how could I divorce and leave them? She would insult me by calling me unemployed. If I was unemployed, why did she marry me? Why didn't she see all this before marriage? Today she has defamed and ruined me to such an extent that I am not in a position to do anything. I want to tell everyone that any unemployed person should think very carefully before marrying a working woman. About 7 months ago, since July, my wife was talking to a person named Sonu Gautam. She said she would only marry him. They had a relationship. I hid many of her mistakes, didn't tell anyone anything. Who can a man share his troubles with? Even the laws in the world are mostly made in favor of women. No one listens to men's side. I am not able to tell my family about my troubles. It causes a lot of pain. Now I am completely helpless. My last wish is that after my death my wife should not touch my body. If possible, my body should be handed over to my family members. Family dispute caused the incident ASP Siddharth said- Before dying, Amaresh had made a video and sent it to his brother-in-law too. Family dispute is being cited as the reason for the incident. Further action will be taken after the post-mortem report comes.

stories.title: Ballia SDM bitten by pet dog seeks 8-day leave:Sends application with thumb impression to DM; travels to Delhi for treatment
stories.summary: In Ballia, SDM Alok Pratap Singh was bitten by a pet dog. He requested 8 days of leave from the DM. He wrote in the application - The dog bit me on both hands, causing deep wounds. I received treatment from a local doctor, but the bleeding from the wounds is not stopping. He further wrote - I am unable to do any of my work. Doctors have advised me to consult a good hospital and a specialist doctor. Therefore, I request permission for leave from March 6th to March 13th. Following this, the DM granted him 8 days of leave. Thumbprint on the application Alok Pratap Singh is the SDM in Bairia Tehsil. He is a 2023 batch PCS (Provincial Civil Service) officer. On March 5, he wrote an application to the DM asking for leave. He put a thumbprint on the letter instead of a signature. DM Mangala Prasad Singh said- A leave application has been submitted. The SDM was bitten by a dog on his hand. He is unable to write due to a plaster cast on his hand. 'I have come to Delhi for treatment' Dainik Bhaskar spoke to SDM Alok Pratap. He said, I have come to Delhi for treatment. My mother and father arrived on the night of March 2nd. My pet dog was excited to meet them. On March 3rd, we were all sitting in the lawn in the morning, drinking tea. My pet dog was barking. I was bringing him towards my parents, holding his leash. Meanwhile, he bit one of my hands with his jaws. To get free, I tried to pull him away with my other hand. This injured both my hands. A staff member present there poured water on the dog from a bottle, and only then did he let go of me. Currently, I am on medical leave. Accused of getting domestic work done Alok Pratap Singh took charge as Deputy Collector in Ballia on February 12, 2024. In January 2026, he was accused by a home guard of being removed from duty, made to do domestic work, and misbehaving. Additionally, a former MLA had raised questions about him regarding the active presence of brokers in the tehsil.

stories.title: Brother-in-law kills sister-in-law in Etawah:Eloped and married; man later informs police about body at home
stories.summary: A 35-year-old brother-in-law killed his 18-year-old sister-in-law in Etawah. 4 days ago, on Holi, he had eloped with his sister-in-law to Delhi. There, they got married in a temple. On Saturday morning, he reached home from Delhi. At night, he argued with his sister-in-law, Sunaina. In anger, he killed her by hitting her with bricks. After the incident, he went to the police station with the blood-stained brick. He told the police officers, "I have committed murder. The body is lying at home. Pick it up." The accused Vijay Kushwaha works as a contract mechanic in the Delhi Jal Board. 5 years ago, he had a love marriage with Nisha Kathariya. At that time, too, they had eloped to get married. Both families had later accepted their relationship. Vijay and Nisha also have a 3-year-old son. 2 months ago, Vijay had a dispute with Nisha. Since then, Nisha had been living at her parents' home. Meanwhile, Vijay got into an affair with Nisha's cousin, Sunaina. The entire incident took place in the Karanpura area of Etawah Kotwali. When police reached the house, blood was scattered in the room After accused Vijay surrendered, the police reached his house. The body was lying on the floor in the room. There was blood scattered everywhere. Police informed Sunaina's family. The body was sent for a post-mortem. Accused Vijay Kushwah's parents live with him in Delhi. Due to having a house and land in the village, he used to come here often. Deceased Sunaina's father, Raghuraj, said, 'Vijay used to visit our house daily'. On March 4, Vijay lured and eloped with our daughter. He took her to Delhi and got married there. We spoke to her on the phone and asked her to come home. On Saturday evening, daughter Sunaina called her mother. She said, 'Mom, we will come home, please don't beat us'. Around 3 AM, we got a call from the police station to come to the district hospital. When we reached there, we saw our daughter lying on a stretcher in the hospital. Vijay had killed her. Vijay is much older than my daughter. Police told us that injury marks were found on her body and rope marks on her neck. Sunaina's brother Shivam said - We had told mom many times not to let Vijay come to the house. But no one listened to us. He came one day before Holi. On the day of Holi, he ran away with my sister. They got married in a temple in Delhi and also sent photos and videos. Met sister-in-law while going to convince wife Shivam said - Vijay's character is not good. 5 years ago, he had also eloped and married our aunt's daughter, Nisha. There has been discord between Vijay and Nisha for the last two months. Vijay often used to come to his in-laws' house in Barra village of Baidpura to convince his wife, Nisha. That's where he met Sunaina. Sunaina's house was also in the same village. Gradually, an affair started between the two. After this, Vijay started meeting Sunaina. Kidnapping case was registered Shivam said - When Vijay took Sunaina on March 4, we filed a kidnapping case against him at the Saifai police station. Station House Officer Inspector Yashwant Singh said that the accused himself informed the police about the murder. After this, he was taken into custody. The matter is being investigated. No written complaint has been received from the family yet. Action will be taken as soon as it is received.

stories.title: 'Sister warned him not to lose career for love':Moradabad man stabbed sister 84 times for girl who was only an online love
stories.summary: In Moradabad, the engineer brother, Hardik, who stabbed his engineer sister 84 times and killed her, has now been sent to jail. During police questioning, he kept making confused statements. He said his Muslim girlfriend was tortured by her family and that her life was ruined because of him. What is shocking is that Hardik (25), who brutally killed his twin sister Himshikha (25) and carried out a deadly attack on his mother for the girl, had never even met her. It was only an online relationship. He used to talk to his girlfriend only on Instagram. CO Civil Lines Kuldeep Kumar Gupta said - During interrogation, Hardik revealed that he had been in a relationship with a Muslim girl from Pune for about one and a half years. They were in touch only through Instagram. They would talk for hours. They had even taken vows to live and die together on Instagram. The police investigation so far has revealed that Hardik wanted to marry his online girlfriend. However, his sister and mother advised him not to be crazy in love, saying this is the age to build a career. Meanwhile, the girlfriend's family also started troubling her. They often started beating her. Police are investigating about the girlfriend. 'Mother was worried alone, so I thought I would kill her' SP City Ranvijay Singh said - After Hardik's arrest, several rounds of interrogation were conducted to understand the motive for murder. However, his behavior appeared psychotic. When asked why he killed his sister, he said, ‘She wanted to control my personal life’. She repeatedly advised me to leave the girl and focus on my career. I tried explaining to her many times to leave me alone, but she wouldn't listen. Sister kept saying what have you become because of one girl. You've even left your job and are always caught up with her. Fed up with my sister's advice and taunts, I killed her. When he was asked why he tried to kill his mother? Hardik said that I thought that after killing my sister, I would go to jail. Mother would be left alone. She would be troubled in that case. So I thought I should kill my mother too. Murdered with vegetable cutting knife Hardik killed his sister with a vegetable cutting knife. After interrogation, the police recovered the knife. Later, he was produced in court, from where he was sent to jail. Meanwhile, the sister's postmortem report came out. A total of 84 wounds were found on Himshikha's body. Heart, liver, kidneys, and ribs were all perforated. There were also 4 knife wounds on the neck. Even her limbs, shoulders, and face had knife wounds. Hardik killed his own twin sister Himshikha with such cruelty and brutality that even the postmortem team was shocked. After the postmortem, Himshikha's dead body was cremated by her maternal uncle Deepu. Police had called relatives by sending information to Badaun. Due to the mother being hospitalized, she could not even see her daughter for the last time. Mother sobbing in hospital, daughter murdered, son sent to jail Mother Neelima is hospitalized after being injured by her son. Hardik had stabbed his mother 6 times with a knife, but Neelima was fortunate to survive. Now her condition is out of danger. In one stroke, Neelima's entire world has been destroyed. Her daughter is dead. Her son is in jail. Thinking about all this, Neelima keeps breaking down in tears on the hospital bed. After killing sister, he told mother, ‘Want to give you a surprise, come home’ According to police, Neelima works as an Assistant Manager at an insurance company office on Delhi Road in Moradabad. On Friday, after killing his sister at home, Hardik went to the office to call his mother. He said, ‘Mom, come home, I want to give you a surprise’. He brought his mother home by car. As soon as the mother opened the gate of the house, blood was spread throughout the house. The blood-soaked, dead body of daughter Himshikha was lying on the bed in the room. She screamed at this. Before Neelima could recover, Hardik launched multiple knife attacks on her as well. Both siblings lived in Gurgaon, brother had quit his job Himshikha and Hardik were twins. After completing engineering, both worked at an IT company in Gurgaon. Himshikha was pursuing an MBA alongside her job. While Hardik also worked at a company for one and a half years. After falling in love with a Gurgaon girl on Instagram, he quit his job and started uploading content on YouTube. Neelima had settled in Moradabad after coming from Badaun According to police, Neelima originally belonged to Jogipur in Badaun. About 30 years ago, she and her husband settled in Moradabad. Around 10 years ago, she separated from her husband. After that, she started living in a rented house in Buddhi Vihar. She educated her children and made them capable of getting jobs.

stories.title: Varanasi woman turns cow dung into livelihood for thousands:Rita Tiwari trains nearly 6,000 women; helps them earn and live with dignity
stories.summary: When intentions are as strong as steel, and the goal is social welfare, even seemingly ordinary resources become a means of extraordinary change. 50-year-old Rita Tiwari, a resident of Tarna Yamuna Nagar Colony in Shivpur police station area of Varanasi district, Uttar Pradesh, has proven this to be true. Today, on the auspicious occasion of International Women's Day, Rita Tiwari's story serves as a beacon for millions of women who dream of creating their own identity and becoming self-reliant. Rita Tiwari has transformed cow dung from mere 'waste' into the foundation of an 'economy'. Today, under her guidance, thousands of women in Varanasi are not only supporting their households but also living with dignity in society by making incense sticks, lamps, statues, and planters from cow dung. The idea of 'empowerment' emerged during crisis Rita Tiwari shares that she has been involved in cow service and social work for the past two decades. However, the major change in her life and working style came during the lockdown imposed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Rita explains that when she would go to poor and Dalit settlements to distribute food, she witnessed the helplessness of women there very closely. Due to financial constraints, these women were struggling even for their children's basic needs. This is where Rita had the idea that these women need not just donations, but work. She contacted the Cow Science and Research Center, Nagpur, and learned the intricacies of making valuable products from cow dung. After training, she ordered molds for making incense sticks, statues, and planters, and began her mission. The beginning was small, but the goal was big. Gradually, women kept joining, and today it has become a caravan. Currently, around 6 thousand women from all eight blocks of Varanasi, like Harhua, Cholapur, Chiraigaon, Badagaon, Pindra, Sevapuri, Araji Line, and Kashi Vidyapeeth have joined this institution.

stories.title: Two women perform last rites for the abandoned in UP:Gorakhpur's 'Pushpalata' Muzaffarnagar's 'Shalu' fulfills duty of a son
stories.summary: Every person desires that when they leave this world, they should be carried by their loved ones. The last rites should be performed with full respect and proper rituals. But not everyone is destined for this. Many people pass away in anonymity, with no one to claim their bodies. Two UP women have taken up the responsibility of giving final farewell to such unclaimed bodies. These women are- Pushpalata Singh from Gorakhpur and Shalu Saini from Muzaffarnagar. On International Women's Day, read the story of these two women of how they chose to step away from social traditions and take up this responsibility, and what inspired them to dedicate themselves to this service. An Ailing Elderly Man Changed Her Life Pushpalata who is a resident of Gorakhpur said that about three years ago she saw an elderly man in a very sick condition by the roadside. She did not leave him in that state. Instead, she brought him home with her and arranged treatment for him. She continued his treatment for nearly a year. Later, the elderly man passed away. She herself performed his last rites and this was the moment when the thought came to her mind that those who have no one in this world also deserve a dignified farewell. From then on, she resolved to perform the last rites of unclaimed bodies. Support for poor and helpless people Pushpalata does not limit herself only to performing the last rites of unclaimed bodies. If she finds any helpless or sick person on the road, she takes care of them and, if necessary, even brings them home with her. 5 thousand people joined, 40 people active She said, “Around 5 thousand people have joined my campaign so far. However, only about 35 to 40 people actively work among them”. Police hands over bodies after legal process According to Pushpalata, bodies that have no claimants are handed over to her by the police after the legal formalities are completed. She then prepares for the last rites with full respect. First, she cleans the body and prepares it properly, and then takes it to the cremation ground located on the banks of the Rapti River. There, she personally carries the body to the funeral pyre and completes the entire ritual by lighting the pyre herself. If someone later gets information about their family member and their last rites have been performed by them, they can also receive the ashes. Pledge to donate own body and organs With this same spirit of humanity, Pushpalata has taken another big decision in her life. She has pledged to donate her body and organs while alive. She said that when she is no longer in this world, what could be more satisfying than having her body or organs be useful for someone in need. Her father is no longer in this world, but even when he was alive, he never opposed this decision. Currently, Pushpalata lives alone in her father's house. More than 250 bodies cremated so far Pushaplata says that in 2025, she performed the last rites of 225 bodies. From the beginning of 2026 until now, she has performed the last rites of more than 50 unclaimed bodies. Now read the story of Shalu Saini from Muzaffarnagar, who has performed the last rites of more than 6,000 bodies from the Covid period until now. Where did the inspiration to perform last rites of dead bodies come from Shalu Saini who is a resident of Muzaffarnagar shares that her social service journey began with a sudden incident. She said, “Dead bodies would often flow into the Ganges river in the Shukratal area. This area is considered a Khadar region, which is why bodies flowing in the river were often found here”. One such day when she saw a body that had flowed into the Ganges, a question arose in her mind about who would perform the last rites of these people. From that moment, she decided to give such bodies a respectful final farewell. Many bodies washed away in Kedarnath floods She said that when disaster struck Kedarnath in 2013, people were washed away to different places. During that time, some bodies arrived in their area. People from her organization informed her about it, then she arranged for their last rites. Performing last rites continuously since Covid period She added, “When the Covid pandemic period came, I started this service work continuously”. She said, “During Covid, the most painful time was when many families were afraid to come near or touch the bodies of their own people. The families who worked hard their whole lives for their loved ones, distanced themselves after death”. She further stated, “At that time, there were very few unclaimed bodies, but now they also receive people who don't have money for last rites or who live in slums”. According to Shalu, from the time of Covid until now, she has performed the last rites of more than 6,000 bodies. Collects expenses with help from friends Regarding the expenses incurred in funeral services, she explained, “I collect money with help of my friends and companions. The work continues with whatever support I receive”. Runs home and service through street vending To support her family, she operates a cart selling clothes and fast food at Jhansi ki Rani Chowk. From this income, she manages both her children's expenses and her social service work. Also started an old age home She said that she had a plot in South Krishna Puri area, where she started an old age home named 'Krantikari Shalu Saini'. Arrangements are being made here to house helpless elderly people. Takes ashes to Haridwar every month She stated that she takes the ashes of the bodies whose last rites she performs to Haridwar every month and immerses them in the Ganges. Peace prayers are also conducted there. Sons Also Help She said that her children are the biggest support in her life. They give her full support and never stop her from doing this work. When she is out of town, her 23-year-old son Sumit Saini also fulfills this responsibility and performs the last rites when needed.

stories.title: LKG student kidnapped in front of grandfather in Prayagraj:2 criminals flee after dragging child into car
stories.summary: On Saturday, an LKG student was kidnapped in broad daylight in Prayagraj. The student was returning home from school. As soon as he got out of the school van, two criminals pulled him into a car and fled. This kidnapping happened in front of the child's grandfather. He had come to receive him. He was standing just a short distance away. The family's financial condition is not good. The child's father works as a security guard in Mumbai. The mother is in a terrible state, crying continuously. No ransom call has been received yet. Additional Police Commissioner Dr. Ajay Pal Sharma and Yamunapar DCP Vivek Chandra Yadav reached the spot. Both officers reprimanded Manda police station SHO Anil Kumar Verma. Ajay Pal has assured the recovery of the student within 24 hours. Police teams are engaged in searching for the kidnappers. Now read the complete incident in sequence... School is 15 km away from home The incident occurred around 4 PM on Saturday evening in Sarai Kala village of Manda. Om Prakash Sharma from the village works as a security guard in Mumbai. His wife, two children, and his father, Nageshwar, live in the village. Among Om Prakash's two children, Prateek is the elder one, 6 years old. He has a younger sister who is 3-years-old. Prateek studies in LKG at Sonar Ka Tara School located in Ramnagar, Meja. The school is about 15 km away from home, and he travels by van. The van drops him about 150 meters away from his house, from where his grandfather picks him up and drops him off. Criminals came in white Alto car Grandfather Nageshwar said - Prateek returns home from school around 4 PM every evening. On Saturday evening, too, I was going to pick him up at the same time. I was about 20 steps away from the point where the school van drops off Prateek. Just then, a white Alto car came and stopped. Two people were sitting in it. One came out of the car and started asking me for directions. At that moment, the van arrived. He explained that as soon as Prateek got out of the van, the person who was asking me for directions quickly ran towards the child. Before I could understand anything, his accomplice moved the car forward, and in the next moment, they pulled Prateek into the car and fled with their companion. I ran after them but couldn't reach the car. Grandfather said - Couldn't see the car number Police arrived after being informed about this incident that occurred in broad daylight. During questioning, the grandfather said that everything happened so quickly that he couldn't see the car number. He had never seen either of the criminals before. When police questioned the villagers, they learned that the car went towards Aunta village. Police set up checkpoints on all nearby roads, but so far no trace of the kidnappers, and the child has not been found. DCP Yamunanagar Vivek Chandra Yadav said, So far in the questioning, the family has not mentioned any enmity. The family's financial condition is not very good. Till now, no calls have been received by the family members. Investigation is being conducted on every point. Akhilesh Yadav demands safe return of the child home

stories.title: YouTuber Anurag Dobhal crashes car during Instagram Live:‘UK07 Rider’ survives high-speed ‘final drive’ in apparent 'suicide' bid
stories.summary: Famous YouTuber from Dehradun Anurag Dobhal allegedly attempted suicide during an Instagram live on Saturday evening. Around 7 PM, he went live while driving his car on the Meerut highway in Uttar Pradesh. During the live session, he appeared emotional and said, “Let’s go for the final drive.” He was also seen slapping himself repeatedly while speaking about his mother. At one point he said, “Next time I come, just give me love.” Soon after, Anurag reportedly accelerated the car to nearly 150 kmph and crashed it into a divider. The Instagram live ended immediately after the collision. Anurag Dobhal is widely known online as UK07 Rider and had also participated in Bigg Boss 17. He sustained injuries in the crash and has been admitted to Shubharti Hospital in Meerut, where he is currently undergoing treatment. See PHOTOS related to the incident... “Mom, give me love when I come next time” In the Instagram live video, Anurag emotionally said, “Mom, when I come in the next life, just give me love… I really needed love. There are no people left now, who should I call?” After saying this, he added, “Let’s go for the final drive.” In the video, he is seen playing an English song in the car and accelerating rapidly. Within moments, the speed touches around 144 kmph. During the drive, he suddenly turns the steering wheel, seemingly attempting to hit the divider. However, the live video abruptly stops at that moment. Second video surfaces, Anurag seen crying on the road Another video from the scene has also surfaced on social media. In the footage, Anurag’s car appears badly damaged, and he is seen lying on the road while people nearby rush to help him. Wearing a yellow T-shirt, Anurag is seen crying in pain as bystanders pull him out of the car and assist him. Had shared emotional 2-hour video four days ago Just four days before the incident, on March 4, Anurag had uploaded a nearly two-hour-long video on his YouTube channel. In the video, he opened up about his personal life struggles, including family disputes, marriage issues, leaving home, financial problems and mental stress. Throughout the video, he became emotional several times and even broke down while speaking. He said his life had changed drastically in recent years and that circumstances forced him to make his personal story public. Anurag also played audio recordings and conversations with family members in the video, stating that he had been dealing with mental stress for a long time.
