stories.title: 8-year-old run over by woman teacher’s car in Lucknow:Child dies; locals surround 3 accused for 30 minutes
stories.summary: An 8-year-old boy was run over by a car driven by a woman teacher in Lucknow, leading to his death on the spot. Angry villagers surrounded the accused teacher and two other women teachers travelling with her. Police reached the spot and calmed the crowd by assuring appropriate action. The three women teachers were later taken to the police station. The incident took place around 4:30 pm on Thursday in Amiliha Kheda village under Mohanlalganj police station area. The deceased has been identified as Arjun, son of Tinkal. The child was standing by the roadside According to eyewitnesses, Arjun was standing near the roadside in the evening when a speeding WagonR car ran over him. He died on the spot. After the incident, villagers gathered at the scene and caught the woman teacher driving the car. Two other women teachers were also in the vehicle, and the crowd stopped them as well. All three female teachers were returning from Raebareli Police said all three women teachers were taken to the police station for questioning. It was found that they teach at a school in Rae Bareli. They travel together by car from Lucknow to the school and were returning when the accident occurred. The body has been sent for post-mortem and further investigation is underway. The female teacher is a resident of Telibagh Police identified the accused teacher as Renu Sanjeev Kumar, daughter of Rammoorti, a resident of Gandhinagar near GS Public School in Telibagh. The police have taken both Renu and the car into custody. The child’s family members are currently at the Mohanlalganj Community Health Centre. Legal action will be taken after receiving a formal complaint from them.

Contractor who threatened HPCL officials shot in encounter in Badaun Ajay Pratap, accused in the murder of HPCL GM and assistant manager, was shot in both legs in a “half encounter” and admitted to the hospital. New DGM returns to Mumbai after incident. 4. SC rejects PIL seeking mandatory menstrual leave says, ‘Nobody will hire women…they will have to sit at home’ The Supreme Court of India on Friday refused to entertain a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking a nationwide policy mandating menstrual leave for women students and employees. 5. Truck crushes 11th-class student in Prayagraj, body found in two parts A student heading to coaching was dragged 25 feet with her bicycle by a speeding truck. Locals caught and beat the fleeing driver. 6. Sambhal CO warns against protests over Iran–Israel conflict during Eid Circle Officer Kuldeep Kumar cautions that anyone disturbing peace or raising foreign-issue slogans will face strict action after concerns over the Iran-Israel conflict. 7. Iran’s Araghchi dials Jaishankar, seeks BRICS co-operation The war involving the United States, Israel and Iran has entered its 14th day. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spoke by phone with India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar about the ongoing conflict and regional security issues, according to Iran’s state news agency IRNA. 8. Agra fashion designer dies by suicide, accuses constable of exploitation The 34-year-old recorded a video alleging harassment and threats from a police constable; her FIR complaints were reportedly ignored. 9. Shia protests in Lucknow; US flag trampled, commandos in Varanasi ahead of Alvida Jumma Following Iran’s Supreme Leader’s death, unrest has led to high alert in UP. DGP Rajeev Krishna orders increased security in sensitive areas. 10. Congress protests with stoves over LPG shortage, online booking halted in MP The US-Israel war with Iran has led to a nationwide shortage of LPG. Long lines are seen outside gas agencies. Black marketing and hoarding of gas cylinders is also taking place.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi says Modi ‘psychologically defeated’:Alleges he has surrendered to the US, not functioning as PM
stories.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said that chanting “Rahul Gandhi Zindabad” does not achieve anything. He said real change comes when a person firmly decides that they will not accept what is happening. Before delivering his speech, he said he was thinking about how Dr B.R. Ambedkar spoke about education and about organising society. He said that today people remember Kanshi Ram, but society has been divided into 15 and 85. According to him, only 15% of people are benefiting, while the remaining 50% have been divided into different groups. Rahul Gandhi said that if Jawaharlal Nehru were alive today, Kanshi Ram would have been the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. He also alleged that Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri’s name appears in the Epstein file. He further claimed that George Soros has invested in a company linked to Puri’s daughter. Rahul Gandhi added that Narendra Modi is no longer acting as India’s Prime Minister and is working for the United States. He said when he was about to raise the issue in Parliament, Modi left the House. Earlier, Congress leaders welcomed him at the airport. This is the first time Rahul Gandhi has come to Lucknow to attend a major event two days before Kanshi Ram’s birth anniversary. Around 4,000 people attended the programme. The event is being seen as a major political move by Congress to strengthen its position among Dalit voters. During the Lok Sabha elections, Congress had contested in alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP). In that election, the number of NDA seats in Uttar Pradesh dropped to 36, while the grand alliance managed to win 43 seats. The alliance now hopes to repeat this success in the 2027 Assembly elections. The Samajwadi Party has also announced that it will observe Kanshi Ram’s birth anniversary as PDA Day. Programmes will be organised at district headquarters in all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on March 15. Congress faces several challenges in UP Congress continues to face multiple challenges in Uttar Pradesh. In Dalit politics, the influence of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) remains strong, especially among the Jatav community, which still has a strong emotional connection with the party. At the same time, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has strengthened its organisation among Dalit communities over the past decade and expanded support through government welfare schemes. Because of this, it may not be easy for Congress to gain a major share of this vote bank. Under BSP-BJP pressure, other parties benefit Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi said that at present the BSP appears to be in its weakest position. The party has no member in the Lok Sabha, only one MLA in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, and it may lose its presence in the Rajya Sabha after December. Both the Samajwadi Party and Congress believe they could emerge as alternatives if the BSP weakens further. While both parties avoid directly calling the BSP weak, they often try to highlight its vulnerability by accusing Mayawati of working under pressure from the BJP. Is BSP really weak? Harshvardhan Tripathi said this perception may not be entirely accurate. Even though Mayawati herself does not appear frequently in public, the party’s organisational network remains active at the grassroots level. Party coordinators are quietly working to strengthen the organisation. The massive crowd that gathered in Lucknow on October 9, 2025, on Kanshi Ram’s death anniversary is seen as evidence of this. According to him, the BSP’s core voter base is again reconnecting with the party.

stories.title: Shia community stages protest in Lucknow, women arrive with children:US flag trampled, commandos deployed in Varanasi; high alert on Alvida Jumma
stories.summary: After the death of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, discontent is being seen in the Shia community. In view of this, a high alert has been issued in Uttar Pradesh on Alvida Jumma. DGP Rajeev Krishna has directed to increase security in sensitive areas. Strict monitoring on social media has also been ordered. Additionally, surveillance is being conducted by drones in sensitive areas. Meanwhile, a 'high alert' has been declared in Bareilly as well. Such tight security arrangements have been made in sensitive areas that not even a bird can fly. In Varanasi today, prayers in mosques will be offered in two shifts. Namaz will be offered amid tight security at Gyanvapi and Latsarayan. Mufti-e-Banaras Abdul Batin Nomani said that Alvida prayers will be offered on the last Friday of Ramadan. Imams and Muezzins will fulfill the tradition of Friday prayers. They will also make supplications in the divine court for the progress and prosperity of the nation. In addition to mosques, tent arrangements will be made on rooftops at several places.

stories.title: Induction stove demand surges amid LPG shortage:From two a month to 25 daily, many shops in Agra report rapid stock depletion
stories.summary: Amid the shortage of LPG cylinders in Agra, the demand for induction stoves has suddenly increased. Where earlier hardly two inductions were sold in a month, now around 20 to 25 induction stoves are being sold daily. Due to increased demand, induction stoves are mostly out of stock in many stores as well as online platforms. The impact of the LPG cylinder shortage is now clearly visible in the electronics market. People in Agra are buying induction stoves as an alternative to gas. Due to the sudden increase in demand, many models are becoming out of stock both online and offline. According to Surendra Chauhan, in-charge of Bharat Business located at Sanjay Place, the sale of induction stoves was very low earlier, and hardly two stoves were sold in a month. But for the last three days, 20 to 25 induction stoves have been sold daily. Meanwhile, many large showrooms in Agra are recording sales of about 30 induction stoves daily. Shopkeepers say that along with induction stoves, the sale of microwave ovens has also increased, as people are looking for alternatives for cooking and heating food. Besides homes, the use of induction stoves has also increased at tea shops and other food stalls. Different companies' induction stoves are available in the market at prices ranging from ₹1,500 to ₹4,000, but due to increasing demand, their stock is rapidly depleting at many shops.

stories.title: Agra fashion designer commits suicide:Accuses constable of exploitation, threats in video; claims police refused to register FIR
stories.summary: A 34-year-old fashion designer died by suicide in Agra after recording an emotional video in which she accused a police constable of exploiting her and threatening her when she sought help. In the video, the woman is seen crying and saying that the constable took advantage of her and later refused to marry her. She claimed she had approached the police station to file a complaint, but no FIR was registered. She also alleged that the constable told her that nothing would happen to a policeman and questioned whether there were any laws to protect women, saying she hoped to receive justice after her death. She ended her life. According to police, the woman had been in a live-in relationship with the constable for nearly 4 years. She reportedly wanted to marry him, but he refused, which left her deeply distressed. On Wednesday night, she was found hanging at her residence. Police said the video surfaced later and went viral, after which action was taken. The accused constable, Jentar Babu alias JB Gautam, has now been arrested and sent to jail. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said that the woman had not submitted any written complaint at the police station earlier. The accused constable works as a computer operator at Tajganj police station. He is a resident of Sardarpur village in Kanpur, while the woman was originally from Kasganj. She was divorced from her husband and had been living with the constable in Agra. The incident took place in the Sainik Nagar area under the Sadar police station. What did the young woman say in the video? Read Police told me, ‘If you file an FIR, you will face trouble.’ Two videos of the young woman have emerged. The first video is 1 minute 13 seconds long. In this, she is saying that one thing has become clear: nothing happens anywhere. Boys can do anything to girls, but nothing happens to boys. I tried to file an FIR at Tajganj police station, but the police said if you file a case, you'll be the one who suffers. Leave it alone, you'll only face trouble. After this, the FIR was not registered. In such a situation, we have no option but to die. Are there no laws for girls? When those who are meant to protect us say nothing can be done, where should we go? I had been living as a wife with JB Gautam for 4 years, but he has made false accusations against me. Constable mentally and physically harassed me The second video is 2 minutes long. In it, she says that the constable's elder brother is telling me to get married, while the constable says his family won't allow the marriage. Don't marry, but at least don't deceive any girl. I am living with him like a wife. Still, I was wrong because he is a policeman. No action is taken against police officers. I have no hope from such laws. JB Gautam and his entire family are the reason for my death. I was mentally tortured. The constable mentally and physically harassed me. I am giving up my life, but I want that person to receive harsh punishment, and I get justice. Divorced husband 6 years ago, then had affair with constable The fashion designer from Kasganj got married 13 years ago. After 6 years of marriage, she got divorced from her husband. After this, the fashion designer started working in a hospital in Agra. During this time, she got acquainted with computer operator (constable) Jenter Babu aka JB Gautam. The two started talking and then had an affair. Both began living in a flat in Tajganj. It is being reported that the fashion designer was pressuring the constable for marriage, but he kept avoiding it. Frustrated by this, the fashion designer complained at the Tajganj police station, but no action was taken. On Wednesday afternoon, the fashion designer went to her younger sister's house at Rajpur Chungi. At night, her sister was sleeping in a separate room with the children, while the fashion designer was in another room. At 12:30 at night, when the sister went to the room, she found the fashion designer hanging from the fan hook. After this, the sister informed the police and family members. Upon receiving the information, the police reached the spot and sent the body for a post-mortem. Family members also arrived after getting the information. The father filed a case at the Sadar police station. Police registered a case for abetment to suicide and establishing relations under false promise of marriage, and arrested the constable. Brother says, ‘Sister did not mention anything at home’ Brother says, ‘We are two brothers and three sisters’. I did not know what kind of problems my sister was struggling with. She had not mentioned it at home either. Sister had done a fashion design course from Lucknow. She was active on Instagram. Several videos with the constable are present on her account. In one video, the constable is seen filling her hair parting with sindoor.

stories.title: Truck runs over 11th class student in Prayagraj:Drags victim for 25 feet along with bicycle; body found in two parts on road
stories.summary: A class 11 student going to coaching in Prayagraj was crushed by a speeding truck. The student was dragged along with her bicycle for about 25 feet. Her body above the waist was split into two. The driver tried to flee leaving the truck after the mishap, but was caught by people, who thrashed him. Police arrived on receiving information about the incident and rescued the driver from the mob and took him to the police station. Meanwhile, angry crowd also vandalized the truck after the incident. Given the seriousness of the situation, police forces from several nearby stations were called to the spot. Police officers are currently trying to control the situation by reasoning with people. The student has been identified as Prachi, daughter of Anand Bahadur Yadav, a resident of Raini village. The student is in class 11 at Adarsh Inter College. The accident occurred at 7 AM in Mailhan village of Phulpur.

stories.title: Cylinder shortage sparks fights in UP:400-meter queue in Lucknow, woman in Kanpur says she feels suicidal
stories.summary: The shortage of cooking gas cylinders in Uttar Pradesh continues unabated. For the fourth consecutive day, people have been facing difficulties. Even after booking, cylinders are not available. Long queues have formed outside gas agencies, and cylinders are being distributed in the presence of police. Meanwhile, a fight broke out in Barabanki over a cylinder. A queue had formed at the gas agency when a vehicle loaded with cylinders arrived. A young man tried to enter the line midway. When another youth attempted to stop him, it led to a scuffle. In Ghaziabad, people created a ruckus over cylinders. As soon as a truck reached the agency, people rushed to collect cylinders. The police somehow managed to control the situation. In Maharajganj, people blocked the road after they were denied cylinders due to lack of booking. The police later convinced them to clear the blockade. In Kanpur, a woman who has been visiting the agency for the past eight days to get a cylinder said she felt like ending her life out of frustration. In Shahjahanpur, ‘Pari Aapki Rasoi’, which provides full meals for ₹10, has been temporarily shut down. In Lucknow’s Gomtinagar Extension, a 400-metre-long queue was seen outside a gas agency. Due to the shortage, demand for induction cooktops and stoves has also increased in the market. Restaurants and hotels are also feeling the impact, and food prices have started rising. In Agra, tea that earlier cost ₹20 is now being sold for ₹25. Black marketing of gas cylinders has also begun in several districts of the state. People are being forced to buy cylinders at double the price. However, gas companies have denied any shortage. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Yogi has directed strict action against black marketing of gas and oil. He has instructed officials to maintain 24-hour monitoring. In view of the gas shortage, the Centre had provided 80 lakh litres of kerosene to the Uttar Pradesh government. The state has a total of 4.26 crore domestic LPG connections, including 1.87 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana. On average, 5 to 6 lakh cylinders are consumed daily in Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: How long will haze remain in UP?:Iran-Israel war behind the fog? Experts answer key questions
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh has remained disturbed for the past 4 days. Dense fog, similar to January conditions, is being seen during the morning hours, with visibility dropping to as low as 30 metres. According to reports, such conditions in March are being observed after 18 years, last seen in 2008. Meanwhile, some people claim that the fog is linked to smoke from the ongoing conflict involving Israel, the US, and Iran. Are these claims true? Will this fog lead to higher temperatures? How long will these conditions continue? To understand this, we spoke with IMD scientist Atul Singh. Get answers to all questions in Bhaskar Explainer… Question 1. Why is there fog in UP? Answer. Two factors work for fog. 1. The air should be stable. 2. There should be moisture in the air. Dry westerly winds were blowing for 5 days. 4 days ago, a cyclonic wind zone formed near Jharkhand. Due to this, winds from the Bay of Bengal reached UP. This fulfilled the moisture deficiency. In this way, all factors for fog formation were completed. Despite the high temperature, fog formed, and visibility remained up to 30 meters. Question 2. What is this change in the weather cycle? Answer. Look, no western disturbance has been active this year. Due to this, there is stability in the air, while western disturbances continue to form in summers. Currently, there is an anti-cyclone over central India. Due to this, there has been a reduction in hot winds. This kept the sky clear, and the heat continues to increase. Question 3. Why are mornings and evenings cold in March? Answer. January and February are winter months. The atmosphere is completely stable during these months. March, on the other hand, is the beginning of summer. Western disturbances start coming during this time. This year, no active disturbance has occurred so far. Although there have been active disturbances in the mountains, this has not happened in the plains. This means that the stability that was formed during the cold has not ended yet. That's why fog is visible. Question 4. Why is dew falling in March? Answer. Usually, winds don't blow from the east during this time. There is also no moisture. However, in March 2026, winds blew from the east. This caused moisture and fog to appear. Now, the eastern winds are gradually clearing up, so the moisture is also reducing. The fog will now start decreasing. Question 5. Has any weather record been set? Answer. It's true that fog in March is rare. However, it's not impossible. This also happened in 2008. Fog had covered the area from March 8 to 10. Question 6. What are the health effects of fog? Answer. Fog can affect children and elderly people. Asthma patients may have difficulty breathing. Small children who spend more time in the dew may face cold and fever issues. However, there is no major harm. Traffic is most affected. One needs to stay alert while driving on roads. Question 7. Will fog have any effect on agriculture? Answer. No, this fog does not have any adverse effect on vegetable and grain production. Question 8. Can it get hotter after fog sets in? Answer. It's true that this season will be hotter. However, fog won't play a role in this. The geographical conditions are such that the El Niño conditions in the Pacific Ocean are gradually moving towards neutral Niño. We can say that the temperature around the equator in the Pacific Ocean is increasing. This will lead to increasing heat in the coming time. Question 9. Is the smoke from Iran-Israel reaching India? Answer. No, that's not the case. These might be discussions among people. But the facts don't support this claim.

stories.title: Lekhpal dies after lying on railway track in Shahjahanpur:Family says, 'he was under stress and undergoing treatment, promotion file pending'
stories.summary: A Lekhpal committed suicide by getting hit by a train. He had returned home after finishing his duty in Shahjahanpur. After this, he went out of the house for some work. During this time, he reached near the railway crossing. He stood near the track waiting for the train. As soon as the train approached, the Lekhpal immediately lay down on the tracks. The train passed over him. His torso was thrown about 25 meters away. After the train passed, the gateman reached him. Police were informed about the incident. Police arrived at the scene and sent the body for a post-mortem. The reason for the suicide has not yet come to light. Police are questioning family members. The incident occurred in the Sadar Bazar area. Amardeep Saxena lived in Bijlipura in the Chauk Kotwali area. He was posted in Garhiya Rangin of Tilhar tehsil. Amardeep returned home from duty late Thursday evening. After staying for a while, he again left home on foot for government work. After this, he directly reached Indranagar railway crossing in the Sadar Bazar area. At that time, the gate was closed. After crossing the gate, he stood near the tracks and started waiting for the train. As soon as they saw the train, they tried to lie on the tracks twice. Then, as the train approached, they immediately lay down on their back on the tracks. The train passed over them. As a result, the body fell far away. The gateman standing there witnessed this entire accident. However, by the time he could understand anything, the accident had already occurred. After receiving information about the incident, police reached the spot and identified the body. The family members were informed about the accident and later arrived at the postmortem house in a state of grief. SDM Sadar and the Tehsildar also reached the spot after getting the news and consoled the family members. According to the family, Amardeep Saxena family includes his wife, Subodhini Saxena, 25-year-old daughter Mitrabinda, and 24-year-old son Kshitij. He was the second among four brothers. Station in-charge Brajesh Singh said that the Lekhpal died after being hit by a train. Police have started an investigation, and further action will be taken based on the complaint from the family. Lekhpal was due for promotion soon Family members said Amardeep Saxena had been under depression for some time. About 3 months ago, his promotion file was sent to the administration, and he was expected to be promoted to Kanungo soon. A few days ago, he had arranged the engagement of his daughter, and preparations for her wedding had begun, although the date had not yet been finalised. Undergoing treatment at AIIMS, posted on SIR duty According to SDM Tilhar Sadanand Saroj, the Lekhpal’s brother informed officials that Amardeep had been undergoing treatment at AIIMS in Delhi for a long time and was under stress due to medication. At present, he was posted on SIR duty in the Katra Assembly constituency.

stories.title: Rahul to mark Kanshi Ram Jayanti in Lucknow:SP also plans events across all 75 districts; focus on Mayawati’s core voters
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi is scheduled to visit Lucknow today, where he will directly interact with around 4,000 party functionaries. The programme comes two days before the birth anniversary of Kanshi Ram and marks the first time Rahul Gandhi is holding a major event in the state capital centred on Kanshi Ram. The Congress gathering will take place at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Gomtinagar. Office bearers from the party’s state unit as well as representatives from its SC, ST and OBC cells are expected to attend. However, the event is limited to organisational members and the general public has not been invited. Political observers see the programme as a significant step by the Congress to reconnect with Dalit voters in Uttar Pradesh ahead of future elections. SP also moves to mobilise Dalit support At the same time, the Samajwadi Party led by Akhilesh Yadav has also announced plans to mark Kanshi Ram’s birth anniversary as “PDA Day”. Party events are scheduled to take place at district headquarters across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh on 15 March. These developments raise a key political question: will the Congress and SP be able to attract Dalit support in the 2027 Assembly elections as they did during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections? Another factor is whether Dalit voters who appeared to return to the Bahujan Samaj Party after a large rally in Lucknow on 9 October 2025 will shift again. Congress seen targeting Muslim–Dalit vote base Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi believes Rahul Gandhi is attempting to consolidate Muslim and Dalit voters. According to Tripathi, Congress currently lacks a stable vote base of its own and is seeking strong backing from these two communities. Together, Muslims and Dalits are estimated to account for around 40 per cent of the electorate. He noted that Rahul Gandhi often visits or attempts to meet Dalit victims in cases of violence, sending a message that the party stands with them. Incidents such as the lynching of a Dalit man from Fatehpur in Rae Bareli and the suicide of a Dalit IPS officer in Haryana were cited as examples where Congress leaders raised the issue publicly. SP also looking beyond traditional support base Tripathi also argues that Akhilesh Yadav recognises that the Samajwadi Party cannot return to power with the support of only OBC and Muslim voters. Within the OBC category, he says, the party’s strongest backing largely comes from the Yadav community. Many non-Yadav OBC groups have moved towards the Bharatiya Janata Party in recent years. As a result, Dalit support has become increasingly important for the SP if it hopes to regain power in Uttar Pradesh. Is BSP really weak? While some political observers describe the BSP as weakened, Tripathi disagrees with the assessment. Although party leader Mayawati maintains a relatively low public profile, he says the party’s grassroots network remains active. According to him, party coordinators continue to work quietly at the local level. The massive turnout at the Lucknow rally on 9 October 2025, marking Kanshi Ram’s death anniversary, suggested that the party’s core support base remains intact and could be consolidating again. Dalit Intellectuals question symbolic politics Dalit thinker and Jawaharlal Nehru University professor Vivek Kumar argues that merely invoking Dalit icons will not automatically win support. He says leaders such as Kanshi Ram gained recognition through long struggles and social movements. Simply displaying their photographs or invoking their names will not persuade voters unless political representation reflects their population share. Kumar also referred to Kanshi Ram’s well-known slogan, “The greater the number, the greater the share,” arguing that parties should demonstrate how they have ensured proportional representation for Dalits in governance and administration. Why Dalit voters are crucial in UP politics Dalits make up roughly 21 per cent of the electorate in Uttar Pradesh. Out of the state’s 403 Assembly constituencies, 84 are reserved for Scheduled Castes. Additionally, in around 40 to 50 other constituencies, Dalit voters constitute between 20 and 30 per cent of the electorate. This means Dalits have a decisive influence in approximately 130 seats across the state. Electoral trends in recent elections In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BJP and its allies won 63 of the 84 reserved constituencies. The Samajwadi Party secured 20 seats, while one seat went to Raghuraj Pratap Singh’s party, Jansatta Dal Loktantrik. During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the campaign in Uttar Pradesh often revolved around the slogan that the Constitution was under threat. In those polls, the SP–Congress alliance won eight of the 17 reserved parliamentary seats, matching the BJP’s tally. Meanwhile, Chandrashekhar Azad of the Azad Samaj Party won the Nagina seat. The SP also secured the high-profile Ayodhya constituency by fielding Dalit leader Awadhesh Prasad. Overall, the NDA’s tally in Uttar Pradesh dropped to 36 seats, while the SP–Congress alliance won 43 seats. The alliance now hopes to replicate this momentum in the 2027 Assembly elections. BSP vote share remains significant Despite a disappointing performance in terms of seats, the BSP still secured 9.84 per cent of the vote in Uttar Pradesh during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Among Dalits, the Jatav community remains the party’s core support base. However, other Dalit groups such as Paswan, Dhobi, Kori and Valmiki voters have increasingly shifted towards the BJP in recent years. Number of voters of each sub-caste among UP Dalits

stories.title: UP records 39°C temperature, light rain likely in 20 districts:Snowfall in Uttarakhand, weather will change here from March 15
stories.summary: UP is experiencing fog and intense heat. The temperature has reached 39°C. Fog was visible for the fourth consecutive day on Friday in 10 districts, including Gorakhpur. Visibility was reduced to 50-100 meters in some places. Meanwhile, snowfall has begun in Uttarakhand. Its direct effect will also be seen in UP. Cold winds will blow in the coming days. The temperature will drop. The Meteorological Department said - besides snowfall in the mountains, a new western disturbance is becoming active. This will start a spell of rain in the state from March 15. There will be intermittent rain in 20 districts, including Kashi-Kanpur. This will be the first rain of the season. This will cause a drop in temperature, which has been running above normal for several days. Cold winds will give a slight feeling of cold. Talking about the last 24 hours, Banda was the hottest city, where the maximum temperature was recorded at 38.8 °C. Besides this, the temperature crossed 37 °C in Jhansi, Agra, Orai, and Hamirpur. There was a surge in temperature in Kashi. After this, the Vishwanath Temple administration has installed German hangers to protect devotees from the sun and heat. Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said - There is a possibility of rain in the eastern and western regions of the state from March 15. During this time, winds will blow at a speed of 30-40 km/hour. The sudden change in weather will cause a drop in temperature. There will be a feeling of mild cold at night. Rain alert in 20 districts, including Kashi-Gorakhpur Atul Kumar Singh says, ‘The main effect of rain can be seen in the Terai regions and Purvanchal’. Light to moderate rain may occur in the Terai region's Lakhimpur Kheri, Bahraich, Shravasti, Balrampur, Siddharthnagar, and Pilibhit, and Purvanchal region's Gorakhpur, Deoria, Kushinagar, Mau, Ballia, Varanasi, Kanpur, Ghazipur, Jaunpur, Chandauli, Basti, Siddharthnagar, Sant Kabir Nagar, and Azamgarh, and surrounding areas. Will fog damage the crops? Devotees won't be troubled by sunlight at Kashi Vishwanath Temple The Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple administration has installed German hangers for devotees. Due to this, devotees standing in line for darshan will get relief from the sun. Actually, the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor is made of stones. After intense sunlight falls on the stones, more heat radiates from them. Devotees have to face many difficulties. The temple administration has taken this decision considering this issue. Chief Executive Officer of Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Vishwa Bhushan Mishra, said - Thousands and lakhs of devotees come daily to have darshan of Baba Vishwanath. This leads to long queues. Sometimes devotees faint and fall down. Keeping this in mind, German hangers have been installed in the temple so that devotees are protected from the sun. They can get relief from the heat. What the weather will be like for the next 4 days... Another sudden reason for fog? Meteorologist Manoj Srivastava from Banaras Hindu University (BHU) said - A low-pressure system has formed between Bihar and Marathwada. Due to this, fog-like conditions are forming in some parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh during morning hours. The wind is blowing close to the surface. Therefore, there has been a slight drop in temperature, but the temperature will increase as the day progresses. He says, 'Due to the upcoming active western disturbance, there will be a gradual drop in the state's temperature from March 14'. From March 15, there will be light rain for the first time this season in the terai regions of the state, along with some parts of Purvanchal. This period will continue for a few days. After that, the temperature will start rising. Why is the heat increasing in March? Skymet Weather's Vice President, Mahesh Palawat, says that in recent years, the effect of climate change has been clearly visible on the weather. Due to this, the weather pattern is changing rapidly. Summer is starting earlier compared to before. The effect is that now the temperature is rising more rapidly. The number of hot days is also increasing. Sometimes the heat wave period also lasts longer than before. In the past few years, many cities in the country have broken old heat records. In some places, temperatures have been recorded above 48 degrees. Heatwave could last for a long time According to IMD's forecast, heatwave conditions may persist for a long time in some areas this year. This means that temperatures could remain very high for several consecutive days in many cities, and people may have to face intense heat. When is it considered a heatwave? According to the weather department, a heatwave is declared when the temperature in the plains reaches 40 degrees Celsius or higher, or when it is recorded 4 to 6 degrees above normal temperature. In such conditions, people's health can be affected, and the risk of heat stroke increases.

stories.title: ‘My fate will be like Rajpal Yadav’s’:Monalisa’s director asks, 'How can I release the film after her conversion?'
stories.summary: 'Monalisa does not know that a storm is coming into her life.' This line from the film The Diary of Manipur was once filmed on Monalisa, the young woman who gained attention as the ‘Kumbh Girl’. Now, according to those associated with her, a storm has indeed arrived in her life. Two days ago, Monalisa married a man named Farman Khan in Kerala. The development has upset her father, Jai Singh Bhonsle, a resident of Maheshwar. At the same time, film director Sanoj Mishra claims the marriage could severely affect the release of his film. Mishra says he has taken a loan of ₹10 crore to finance the project and now fears the controversy surrounding Monalisa may jeopardise its prospects. According to Mishra, the film addresses the issue of religious conversion. He believes Monalisa’s marriage to a Muslim man has created a situation that could make the film’s release difficult. Director says he learned of the marriage through news Speaking to Bhaskar in an exclusive interview, Mishra said he first heard about the marriage when someone sent him a news report yesterday afternoon. He said, ‘At first I thought it might be a media stunt connected with a film shoot, but when the situation began to escalate, I contacted her father.' Mishra said that at the time, Jai Singh Bhonsle was standing outside a police station in Kerala while Monalisa was inside. He asked to speak with her so he could try to persuade her, but police reportedly did not allow him to meet her. Later, he was told that the police had taken Monalisa out through the back entrance, which made him realise the matter was serious. 'She travelled to Kerala for film offer' Mishra said Monalisa had told him about a week earlier that she needed to travel to Kerala for a film opportunity. According to him, she claimed she had signed a project in which she would play the role of a captain. He also said her father had been offered a role as her father in the film. The plan was to spend about ten days there for training before the shooting began. ‘I even told her that if she did not know Hindi properly, how would she speak Malayalam or Tamil?’ Mishra said, adding that they had no professional network in that region. According to him, neither he nor her father suspected anything unusual at the time. Concerns about film’s future and financial loss Responding to claims that Monalisa took the step because her father wanted her to marry a relative, Mishra said he had never heard about such an issue during the period they were working together. He said they had been shooting for the film until two months ago and that he had a close, family-like relationship with her. ‘If such a situation existed, she would have told me,’ he said. Mishra added that he has invested heavily in the project and is worried about the financial consequences. According to him, two years of work, a loan of ₹10 crore and even a period spent in jail during the project have all been put at risk. 'My film was against religious conversion. Now the heroine herself has converted, how can I release the film in this situation?' he said. Training and investment in the actress Mishra also said he spent considerable effort training Monalisa for acting. During his 35-year career, he claimed he had never invested as much time and resources into preparing an actor. He said around ₹42 lakh was spent over one and a quarter years on her training. Trainers were brought from Mumbai, and to ensure she did not have to stay away from home, accommodation for her entire family was arranged in Ujjain. He said that at present his main concern is repaying the loan, which was taken for eight months and now has only three months remaining before repayment is due. Father describes events in Kerala Monalisa’s father, Jai Singh Bhonsle, also spoke to the media about the events leading up to the marriage. He said he had previously met Farman Khan when the latter had approached them about making a film featuring Monalisa. There were discussions about signing a project, but the plan was eventually cancelled and the two families lost contact. However, according to the father, communication resumed about 20–25 days ago when Farman began speaking to Monalisa on the phone. He reportedly told them she needed better training in acting. Father says they were made to wait outside police station Bhonsle said that when they travelled to Kerala, they were not allowed to enter the police station and had to sit on the road outside for around two and a half to three hours. When he was briefly able to speak with Monalisa, she reportedly said she wanted to learn dance and acting and did not wish to return to the village. Responding to allegations that he wanted her to marry her aunt’s son, Bhonsle denied ever discussing marriage for his daughter, saying she is still young. He said the family finds it difficult to believe that a relationship developed in just a few days and suspects that Monalisa may have been influenced in some way. Appeal to daughter to return home Through the media, Monalisa’s father appealed to her to return home. He said that if any mistake had been made under someone’s influence, she should apologise to society. The family’s primary concern, he said, is her safety and well-being. They expressed hope that the government would assist in resolving the matter and ensuring that their daughter returns home safely.

stories.title: Contractor who threatened 2 HPCL officials killed in encounter:Accused shot in both legs; new DGM flies back to Mumbai after incident
stories.summary: A major revelation has come in the murder of Hindustan Petroleum's GM Sudhir Gupta (55 years) and Assistant Manager Sales Harshit Mishra (35 years) in Badaun. Police caught the murder accused in a “half encounter.” The accused contractor, Ajay Pratap, was shot in both legs during the operation. After that, the police carried him on their shoulders to the vehicle and took him to the district hospital, where he was admitted for treatment. Sudhir Gupta had filed an FIR against Ajay Pratap Singh at the Moosajhag police station on February 4. He alleged that Ajay was constantly threatening him and stalking him. The DGM was so scared that he had submitted his VRS application 5 years before retirement, which was approved. March 31 was his last day of service. He had hidden the weapon in the forest while fleeing. Police took him to the forest to recover it. During this time, the accused pulled out a loaded country-made pistol from the bushes and opened fire. Police retaliated, and the accused was shot in both legs. Since Ajay was a village strongman with political connections, the police took no action. On Thursday, when the contractor entered the plant and committed double murder, the police suspended Station In-charge Ajay Kumar and beat In-charge SI Dharmendra Kumar in an attempt to cover up. The investigation was handed over to CO City Rajneesh Kumar Upadhyay. People say that Ajay's terror extended from the village to the plant. Whenever he wished, he would enter the plant and threaten officers. If police had taken action in time, both officers' lives could have been saved. Read what the DGM had stated in his complaint... DGM Sudhir Gupta filed an FIR at Musajhag police station on February 4. The newly appointed DGM, who had arrived to take charge, was frightened by the incident and returned to Mumbai. According to reports, the new DGM, Lokesh, had reached the plant on Thursday to assume charge. The incident occurred in front of him, which left him shaken. Police later dropped him at Bareilly airport, from where he left for his home in Akola, Mumbai. 1. Forcefully entered the plant on January 13, says, ‘will teach everyone a lesson.’ Ajay Pratap Singh, a resident of Sainjani village, was a contract employee at Lakshya Powertech. He has repeatedly created criminal activities, threats, and an atmosphere of fear in the CBG plant. The CBG plant is a restricted area declared by the Uttar Pradesh government. On January 13, around 3:45 PM, Ajay Pratap Singh forcefully took control of another contractor's (engineering consultant) taxi and forcefully entered the CBG plant premises. He came to the conference room inside the plant. He threatened the HPCL officers who were having food, saying, ‘he would teach everyone a lesson’. 2. Showed knife wounds on body; employees got scared Ajay Singh also claimed that he is connected to a gangster group based in Noida. He has worked for them for many years. He also showed many knife marks on his body while claiming to be a member of Shahjahanpur's gangster group. This scared the officers and employees. 3. Stopped the car and threatened me On February 4th itself, around 5:45 PM, when we were returning from the office, Ajay Pratap Singh forcefully stopped our car by raising both hands in the middle of the road at Sainjani intersection, after the CBG plant, and then threatened us. 4. Barged into the location In-charge's Office, and shouted loudly On January 14th morning at 11:10, Ajay Pratap Singh forcefully entered the plant again. He barged into the location-in-charge's office and kept shouting and giving threats loudly. When HPCL officials were going to meet authorities to file a complaint about this, he again forcefully stopped HPCL's taxi inside the plant premises, blocked the way, and gave threats. 5. Chased for several kilometers and stopped When HPCL officials left in another contractor's vehicle, he chased them on his bike for about 5 kilometers. He overtook them multiple times and rode alongside while continuing to give threats. The staff have previously made several complaints to HPCL management about the hooliganism of Ajay Pratap Singh and his associates. He has openly threatened HPCL contractors. 6. If anything happens, Ajay Singh will be responsible In this case, a case should be registered against Ajay Pratap Singh under charges of forcibly entering the plant, giving threats, forcibly stopping vehicles, etc. Strict action should be taken against him to prevent any untoward incident in the future. In the future, if there is any threat or harm to the life of any HPCL officer, employee, or their lives, Ajay Pratap Singh will be fully responsible for it. Manager's father says - Collusion between HPCL Operation Head and accused Assistant Manager Harshit's father, Sunil Mishra, alleges that the murders happened because of HPCL Operation Head Rajeev Kumar Singh. It's his entire conspiracy, because he came here on a visit on March 10th, and today the murder happened. The accused, Ajay Singh, received a call from Rajeev Singh. If his phone is seized, everything will become clear. I will ensure Rajiv Singh gets punished. If it were an attack, all officers would have been killed, but here, only two officers were killed. Because the security guards at the gate let the accused go without searching. This is all part of Rajiv Singh's conspiracy. Now he is sitting with his phone switched off. Now know the sequence of the double murder... Accused Ajay Pratap Singh arrived at the plant in a Bolero around 1 PM on Thursday. 6 people were sitting in the Bolero, including Ajay. These included 4 plant employees and a driver. The employees' shift was from 2 PM. The Bolero was not checked at the time of plant entry. Ajay had arrived with an automatic gun. He opened rapid fire on Sudhir and Harshit. Both died as a result. According to eyewitnesses, Sainjani resident Ajay Pratap Singh forcibly entered the plant with some people. He started abusing Sudhir and Harshit's colleagues. Both officers opposed him. Meanwhile, Ajay started firing. Both officers standing in front were hit by bullets and fell down injured. After this, the accused fled from the scene. Police arrested him after some time. In the evening, ADG Ramit Sharma and DIG Ajay Kumar Sahni inspected the crime scene. Sudhir Gupta was a resident of Noida Sudhir Gupta's father's name is Dayakishan. He was originally from Silver Estate Apartment, Sector-50, Noida. Currently, he was living in front of the Sanjay Community in Bareilly. Meanwhile, Harshit Mishra is from Puranpur in Pilibhit. Late in the evening, Harshit's family arrived in Badaun from Pilibhit. Accused's brother was a district panchayat member Accused Ajay alias Ramu has two brothers. Their names are Michku and Shekhar. Ramu has two sons and one daughter. He has 6 shops near the village. He owns about 35 bighas of land. Ramu's cousin Abhay Pratap has served as a district panchayat member. He is said to be close to a BJP MLA. Accused Ajay Pratap Singh is the uncle of the Sainjani village head. His mother, Kiran Devi, is a ration shop dealer. The plant is also in his village.

stories.title: Gas crisis shuts bangle and petha factories in UP:30K workers unemployed in Bulandshahr; 8K Meerut units in trouble
stories.summary: The impact of the America-Israel and Iran war is being felt in Uttar Pradesh’s pottery, bangle, and petha industries due to a shortage of gas supply. The worst impact is in Asia’s largest pottery hub in Bulandshahr, where 95% of the 300–325 pottery units have shut down, leaving over 30,000 workers unemployed. A similar situation is seen in Firozabad’s bangle factories and Agra’s petha units, where furnaces have gone silent due to the gas shortage. In Agra, 40 of the 55 large petha factories have already closed. If gas supply does not resume soon, Agra’s silver anklet industry could also face a major crisis. Khurja’s pottery industry hit by gas price surge After Japan and England, Khurja in Bulandshahr has Asia’s largest pottery industry, with over 300 units employing more than 30,000 workers. The industry generates around ₹100 crore in business every month in domestic and international markets. However, due to the war in the Gulf region, the situation has changed rapidly. A sudden rise in gas prices and supply issues has forced pottery entrepreneurs to stop production. Ravi Rana, president of the Khurja Pottery Association, says gas prices have increased two-and-a-half times. As per the agreement, PNG costs ₹49 per kg, but if consumption exceeds the agreed limit, the rate rises to ₹119.90 per kg. At the same time, LPG prices have increased from ₹61 to ₹93 per kg. Gas supplier companies have informed buyers about the price hike through email. Due to these higher costs, many entrepreneurs have shut their pottery units and halted clay utensil production. Entrepreneurs allege that companies are arbitrarily fixing rates. They say pottery units can only run on PNG or commercial LPG, as the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has banned the use of kerosene, diesel, and coal. In these conditions, many owners see continuing production as a loss-making venture, making closure the only option. With the shutdown of units, around 30,000 workers have lost their jobs, putting their livelihoods at risk. Abhishek Kumar, a worker from Deoria, says the factory where he worked has shut down. “We came here to earn. If this situation continues, we will have to return home,” he says, adding that thousands of labourers are facing the same problem. “If the factory doesn’t run, what will we do by staying here?” Firozabad's Bangle Industry: Production reduced by 30 to 40% Firozabad’s world-famous glass and bangle industry is facing a crisis due to reduced gas supply and rising prices. Production has declined in many factories, several units are on the verge of closure, and thousands of labourers are facing an employment crisis. Industrialists say the industry normally receives about 1.5 million cubic meters of natural gas daily from GAIL Gas Limited. After the war began, the supply was first reduced by 0.3 million cubic meters, and later the remaining quota was also cut by around 20%. A meeting of the Uttar Pradesh Glass Manufacturers Syndicate (UPGMS) decided to reduce production. Automatic factories making glass bottles and bangle tank furnace units have cut production by 30–40%, while pot furnace factory owners have decided to stop production completely. Entrepreneurs say that along with expensive gas, raw materials and chemicals have also become 15–20% costlier. As a result, bangles cannot be sold at old prices, and the price has increased by ₹5–10 per ‘toda’ (bundle of 60 bangles). However, buyers are scarce at the higher prices. Binny Mittal, president of the Industrial State Cooperative Society, says the industry is in crisis after the gas quota cut. Many entrepreneurs are waiting for their gas bills and have reduced or halted production until the situation becomes clear. Many factories are now considering closure. GAIL Gas has informed industries by email about the supply cut and warned of penalties for excessive use. Labour organisations have also expressed concern. Ramdas Manav, general secretary of the Glass and Bangle Workers’ Union, says factories are again facing closure after Holi. If the situation does not improve soon, 5–7 lakh labourers in the district could face a livelihood crisis, and the city’s glass and bangle industry may face a serious downturn. Agra's Petha Industry: 40 out of 55 big factories closed The petha industry in Agra is facing a crisis due to gas shortages. Businessmen say furnaces are not running because gas cylinders are unavailable, affecting production and pushing small petha factories to the verge of closure. Rajesh Agarwal, president of the Shaheed Bhagat Singh Petha Cottage Industry, says Agra has 55 large petha factories, and about 40 gas-based units at Noori Darwaza have already shut down. Thousands of artisans are sitting idle, and if the situation does not improve, recession-like conditions and even starvation could arise. Silver industry may stop work soon Nitesh Agarwal, president of the Agra Sarafa Association, says there are around 800 silver jewellery factories, most involved in making anklets. Silver melting and soldering require gas. Work is continuing for now, but he warns that if cylinders are not supplied within one or two days, work in more than half the factories will stop. Meerut: 50 factories closed, 8,000 affected In Meerut, gas shortages are affecting the plastic, wire, glass, and paint industries. So far, 50 units have stopped production, while over 8,000 factories are struggling due to shortages of gas and oil. Industrial areas like Mohkampur, Partapur, Udyogpuram, Vishwakarma Industrial Area, and Dhyanchand Nagar have major chemical, plastic, wire, and glass factories, and work there has been affected. Rajeev Agarwal, vice chairman of Meerut IIA, says concerns are rising in industrial areas and there is also a shortage of commercial cylinders. Kanpur: 150 pipeline-gas factories shut In Kanpur, Vijay Kapoor, chairman of the Kanpur Industrial Development Co-operative Estate Limited, says industries could face losses worth billions of rupees if supply is not restored soon, putting the livelihoods of around one lakh people at risk. He says the gas shortage has severely affected factories. Most units depend on commercial cylinders, while about 150 large factories receive gas through pipelines, but their supply has currently stopped, pushing them towards closure.

stories.title: Sambhal CO warns against protests over Iran–Israel conflict:Says, 'anyone disturbing peace during Eid or raising slogans over foreign issues will face strict police action'
stories.summary: Circle Officer Kuldeep Kumar made the remarks during a Peace Committee meeting held in the Asmoli area of Sambhal district. Referring to the ongoing Iran-Israel conflict, he said that some people appear overly concerned about the issue and warned them not to create disturbances locally over international matters. He added that if anyone has such strong feelings about the conflict, they should go and support the country they favour instead of disturbing peace here. He also warned that the police would take strict action against anyone attempting to disrupt law and order. A video of the meeting has also surfaced. The meeting was organised at Sambhal Kotwali on Wednesday ahead of Alvida Jumma and Eid. Since the regular CO of Sambhal is on leave, Kuldeep Kumar was also handling the charge. City Magistrate Sudhir Kumar and Inspector Gajendra Singh were present during the meeting. During the discussion, the officer appealed to members of the Muslim community to celebrate the festivals peacefully and emphasised that the city’s peace should not be disturbed in the name of international conflicts. Read what else the CO said Go board the plane going to Iran CO Kuldeep Kumar says, ‘Some people are very troubled here by the Iran-Israel war’. They are beating their chests here. If you have so many problems, then get on a plane and go there. These are all international issues. We don't need to get involved in what's happening in Bangladesh? Khamenei was killed in Iran? Sir, America is committing atrocities? Look, there are 56 Islamic countries; they will take care of themselves. If prayers are offered on the road, they will not be forgiven CO says, ‘When there is no space in the mosque, worshippers rush and start praying on the road’. If this happens, we won't say anything for one minute. After that, we will file a case and send them to jail. If anyone shows support or raises slogans for the Iran-Israel war, they will be sent to jail. If disputes from another country affect our country's law and order, the police will give a 'very good treatment'. During prayers, there should be no slogans, banners, or strips against any other country. Kuldeep Kumar says, ‘We are Hindustani, we are Indian’. We are living here peacefully. International issues are for governments to handle, not for common people. If 10 people are standing somewhere beating their chests saying Iran has been killed, then brothers go there and fight. Action will also be taken where posters are made The CO warned that police will take action not only against protesters but also at places where these controversial posters and slogans are printed or written. We are living here peacefully. No one will be allowed to spoil the atmosphere on their own land. The festival is about love and harmony. It's a festival of sweet vermicelli. No bitterness should be mixed in it. Don't let anyone in your area do anything that would spoil the environment. Strict action against REEL makers on social media CO warned social media reel makers, saying, ‘some people say anything just to make Instagram reels’. They spread rumors about issues in foreign countries. Such things will not be tolerated at all. We should not be concerned about what is happening in other countries. Those are their issues, not ours. We must not let our area's atmosphere get spoiled. One 'mischievous' person is enough to spoil the entire environment. Therefore, all responsible citizens should remain alert and cooperate with the police. The meeting was attended by council member Ibrahim, council member's husband Azeem Abbasi, Haji Ehtesham, and Mo. Nazim, Danish Khan, Mohammad Zia, Nabeel Ahmad, Shabban Khan, Akhtar, Idrees, Rashid, along with many other prominent people of the district. Around 50 people participated in the meeting. AIMIM UP President says, ‘Your language is like a street criminal.’ AIMIM's UP President Shaukat Ali has reacted to CO Kuldeep Kumar's statement in Sambhal. He says, ‘CO Kuldeep Kumar is making threats in the peace committee meeting’. If we do anything that is unconstitutional, then file a case. You are sitting and threatening Muslims. The first case should be filed against you. He said that you have considered Muslims weak. Everyone will come and threaten Muslims and leave. Earlier, CO Anuj Chaudhary did the same thing. He shot Muslims. He became a hero. Shaukat Ali says, 'It doesn't seem from anywhere that you have taken the oath of the Constitution'. Your language doesn't sound like an IPS officer's language; it sounds like the language of a street criminal. CO, sir, if you have a problem with us, then you go to Nepal.
